journey.howSecured:
1. Online Assessment Round [137 students appeared for this round ]

This was the initial screening phase which consisted of three sections:

a. Aptitude Section (15 questions) b. CS Fundamentals (20-30 questions) c. Coding Section (2 questions)

The aptitude section consisted of pattern recognition, profit and loss, ratios, statistics. In the CS Fundamentals section questions were based on Core CS, DBMS, OS, SQL and questions based on output prediction using flowcharts/ code snippets. The coding section had two questions as follows:

I. Given an array of integers, find out which numbers would be at the same place and which numbers would have changed positions after sorting the array. (I was able to pass all but one test cases i.e. 9/10)

II. Given a range of numbers X, Y you had to find the sum of all golden numbers. A golden number would be defined such that the sum of its digits - maximum digit out of all digits is equal to the maximum digit. (eg: 3003: sum = 6, max_digit = 3, sum - max_digit = 3). (I was able pass 9/12 test cases)

Important Tips for OA:

1. Time management is the most important aspect of an OA. You must attempt easy and especially short questions first and then go to longer ones. Understand what the question is asking before jumping to the answer and sometimes just try option elimination if nothing works.

2. Keep 30-45 seconds at the end reserved for unattempted questions. This time is basically for those questions that you have absolutely no idea how to answer. You quickly select random options for these and since there are no -ve marks make sure to attempt each question.

3. For aptitude questions refer to IndiaBix and make sure to study up on statistics formulas as they are usually asked in IDFC OAs.

4. For the coding section, the questions for any company are never straightforward; they will give some kind of a pointless story which will take you a minute or two to read and some more minutes to comprehend. These won't be your typical LeetCode questions. I would suggest that toward the end of your preparation phase practice a few of these questions by asking ChatGPT to generate such lengthy story based company OA style questions.

2. Technical Round 1 [40-45 students were selected for this round]

The round started with the interviewer asking me to take him through my resume. Keep this about 60-90 secs max. Then from my introduction he picked up my experience in python and started asking me questions on the language. These basic to in depth questions about the language and its working. He asked me about break, continue & pass, list vs tuple, lambdas, docstring, memory management, garbage collection in python etc. I managed to answer almost all them. The main reason was that I had studied the "Python interview questions" from GeeksforGeeks and most of the questions were exactly the same or similar to it so make sure to study those. Then he asked me some questions on C++ like virtual functions, friend keyword, multiple inheritance and the diamond problem etc. Then he asked me if I knew anything about Operating Systems to which I said I had basic understanding of multithreading and processes which was taught to us in our academics and in theory. He asked me how to run a python program on a UNIX server which I did not. Then he asked about thrashing in an OS which I again wasn't aware of. Next he moved on to DBMS and Schema design. He gave me a situation where I had to design the schema for a hotel which took bookings from customers on their own website and aggregators like MakeMyTrip, TripAdvisor etc. I designed the schema and at each stage communicated with the interviewer on my choice and he would give me hints and direct me if I was drifting in the wrong direction. After a lot of cancellations and reiterations I arrived at the final schema. Keep in mind to keep explaining why you were adding certain tables or columns in your schema. Next he asked to write an SQL query to find the number of room bookings in each quarter which I wrote very easily. He then asked me to update this to find the percentage occupancy in each quarter. He then connected this database scenario to techno-hr questions. He put me in a situation where if I got a call from a customer saying that they had booked a room and made the payment but did not receive a confirmation what would I do. Then he changed it to the booking type being a third party aggregator and the booking of the customer was the next day. I connected this with a situation which I had actually faced during the Coldplay concert in Ahmedabad where our hotel denied us the online booking we had done after reaching there. After he was satisfied with all my answers and a few follow ups, he was finally done and asked me if I had any questions. Make sure to prepare 2-3 good questions based on the company for this beforehand as this creates a great impression and shows that you are serious about the company. I asked him about the GenAI and ML projects that the company had been working on and would be undertaking for internal tools as well as consumer facing tools.

PRO Tips for Technical Rounds:

1. Make ChatGPT your friend as there is no better tool for interview preparations.

2. Know your resume forwards and backwards without missing a single piece of information. Also prepare for in-depth questions for each part of the resume. Sometimes an interview might take a point in your resume and ask very in-depth questions to test your understanding. Use ChatGPT for this and ask it to give curveball questions too.

3. Make sure to keep the points in your resume as honest as possible and don't mention something you lack understanding in. If extremely necessary to include a part you might not know about, make sure to understand it in-depth one day before the interview. Keep in mind that the interviewer is sitting with a laptop and you're not.

4. I would advise that you learn OOPs concepts in Java as a lot of companies have Java as a requirement or at least have some projects of Java in their systems. Then learn those same concepts in your preferred language.

5. For each language you mention in your resume, go through its interview questions from GFG because a lot of times they cover almost everything about the language.

6. Technical Interviews are as much a psychological game as they are about your technical skills. The interviewers will ask you questions on what you have mentioned in your resume and based on what you answer. Make sure to drop hints of where you want to lead them. A lot of the time they might end up asking exactly that.

7. Be confident and honest in your answers and if you are asked something you don't know or to write a code whose syntax you do not recall, try explaining the concept and approach and related concepts you know. Most of the time that is what interviewers are looking for. If there comes a point where you have absolutely no clue of what you are asked, just be straight with them and say that you haven't learnt or worked with this particular concept instead of making up a useless explanation.

8. This is to be followed for all interviews and this is one of the most important aspects of an interview, keep a good eye contact with the interviewer. This might not seem like anything but it conveys that you are confident in your abilities and your answers, otherwise you come across as underconfident especially during HR interviews.

3. Technical Round 2 [ 22 students were shortlisted for this round ]

The round again began with a typical "Introduce yourself". Then they gave me scenarios and told me to identify what data structures would be used in those scenarios. The first scenario was that there were usernames and each had details which would have to be accessed so what DS would be used to which I answered HashMap for O(1) lookups. Then he updated the scenario such that the details of the user would need to be updated constantly. I was still adamant on using a HashMap since lookups would be O(1) but that was not what they wanted. After the interview I realized that they were expecting me to consider this as a normal database and looking for the answer to be B-Trees which are used for data storage in SQL and NoSQL Databases. Next they moved on to OOPs where they asked me to write one or two codes in Java. Next they jumped to Exception Handling and asked me what it was in Java. I told them about checked and unchecked exceptions and try catch. They asked me if it was possible to create custom exceptions in Java and then asked me to write code for a custom exception. I did not remember the exact syntax but I still wrote what I remembered and then explained it to them. Then I was asked about the difference between Exception and RuntimeException and why I inherited the RuntimeException class in my custom exception class. Next came questions on Object class of Java and what equals method is in Java. I knew about Object class being

the topmost class of Java which all classes inherited from but was not aware of equals so told them it was a method of the String class then they said it was of Object class. Now they moved on to 1-2 questions from my resume. I was asked why I used the Llama2 Model in my internship to which I explained about the company's requirements of privacy and budget constraints. Then they saw Git and GitHub and asked the main difference between them. Then they gave a situation where there are two branches one is the main branch and another is the dev branch where a feature was being developed. Say a developer was working on a feature in the dev branch and a constraint was to be created that they could push the code automatically once there were no merge conflicts. I suggested using admin approval before the code was pushed but they wanted it to be done automatically to which I did not know the answer.

Additional Tips for Technical Round:

1. Prepare a clear introduction of yourself well before the interviews. Don't ever think that you can wing it, but at the same time do not rote the intro, prepare points that you want to convey and define a clear flow.

2. Keep your introduction short but make it a story where each point connects to the next and relate it to the role. Also set clear boundaries about what you do and don't know in the intro itself. For example I had used Python for ML and data projects, C++ for DSA and recently learnt Java only for OOPs so I made this very clear in the introduction. This ensures that the interviewer doesn't ask you anything out of scope. The more generalized your introduction is, the more curveballs you could potentially face.

3. HR Round [ 9 students were shortlisted for this round ]

This was your typical HR interview where the interviewer was trying to get to know you and understand if your values aligned with that of the company's. The interview started with her asking me the purpose of this HR interview. Next she asked me to tell her about my resume and something that wasn't in it. Then she asked me about the challenges I have overcome. I was asked what my ideal company would look like where I would enjoy working at. Then I was asked about my ideal manager who I would love to work with to which I connected to my experience where I had talked to a senior of mine who was working at IDFC currently and the way he helped me, worked like a charm. Then I was asked what I knew about IDFC and why I wanted to work there. Next came the Work from home vs Work from office question. I was asked what my thoughts were about both of them and which of them I believed in, be sure to support your answer with adequate reasoning. Then she gave me a situation where I was the team lead for a project for a very important stakeholder who had given us a hard deadline but I found out that it would be impossible to deliver at that date. What would be my approach to this, providing a buggy software which would work for a few days and the client would be happy for now and then it would break down at a later date or do you delay the launch and take the heat but deliver the complete software. Now comes another situation where my manager does not assign me to any important projects or any meaningful work for that matter so what would be my approach to this. I told her about being direct in this situation and confronting my manager and politely explaining the situation. She said what if he/she doesn't give me the time of day to confront them. After she was satisfied with my answer she asked me about my experience at Oculus as a Marketing head and what challenges I faced while leading such a large team. Finally she told me there was one last question or at least that's what she told me. She asked me about my weakness and then based on that created situations. She asked me what if my manager was someone who micromanaged me constantly and check in every 10 minutes what I would do. She reiterated various aspects of this scenario and told me she was done

with the interview after she was satisfied with all my answers. Finally she told me if I had any questions and I asked a couple of questions and I was done.

PRO Tips for HR Round:

1. Think of HR round as a chess match where you have to constantly think, react and plan ahead for every move you make, with the addition that your moves are being constantly judged. My interviewer was someone who was in the HR industry for 15 years and yours would also probably be someone with the same experience so they know people very well, so always be on your guard and say things that actually do align with what you believe in.

2. Be honest but not too honest. This might seem confusing but HR representatives can usually identify when you're lying very easily. Now for the not too honest part, whatever you answer though the actual reason might be something else, mention that, but additionally connect it to the company's values and requirements. For example, for the work from home question some of you might prefer that but the company has work from office policy so align your answer such that you believe in work from home but are open to work from office.

3. Align your answers with the company values and your own experiences. Why this is important is because when you just state facts as an answer but you connect it with an actual experience, it becomes a story which always has great value in interviews not just HR but technical ones too.

4. Another important tip which will help you navigate HR easily is not to keep it one way where they ask and you answer. Try keeping it two-way where you ask them questions based on their questions and your answers and if you are confident enough try adding in a funny remark or two to make the atmosphere less tense.

5. Remember the names of your previous interviewers as it might be asked during HR and it is also a good practice to know it if you do get selected. Usually each interviewer introduces themselves at the start itself but in case someone does not, make it a practice to ask their names at the end of the interview.

3. Final Screening Round [ 9 students were shortlisted for this round ]

This interview was taken by the senior management of IDFC and it was more of a formality but still do not take this lightly as one student was eliminated in this round. The interview was online where the interviewer asked me to take him through my resume. I had a project where I had used Selenium so he asked what Selenium was, what it was used for and what was its use case in my project. Then he asked how I usually approached any problem I was given. Then he came to time complexity analysis and asked what it was. He then asked me the purpose of the big O notation and then asked me if I had to find the time complexity of an algorithm how I would approach that. He then asked a couple of questions which I do not remember and then he asked if I had any questions and that was it.

8 students were offered the job at the end

I was one of the first people to start DSA during the start of 3rd year but then left it

midway for almost the entire Sem 5. Do not make this mistake, once you start make it a habit to do DSA everyday even if it is just one question.

2. You can follow a sheet like Striver's A2Z Sheet or NeetCode or do a combination of both like I did. Start with Striver's SDE Sheet or NeetCode 150 whichever you are comfortable with if you feel confident about Data Structures or go for A2Z Sheet or NeetCode 250 if your basics aren't clear. For Recursion, DP and Graphs make sure to strictly follow Striver and his respective playlists on the topics as it is the best resource on the internet for these topics. The rest you can do from either.

3. Another aspect of DSA is explaining your approach. You may be amazing at DSA but if you cannot explain your approach none of it is any use. When practicing LeetCode, although this might take additional time, but try explaining your approach in your head while you are solving the question

Try to do LeetCode contests if you have the time or you complete DSA early enough to practice time management and make sure to practice company style story based questions for OA practice using ChatGPT. journey.howSecured:
1. Online Assessment

The OA had 3 sections

- Aptitude (20 mins)

- Computer Fundamentals (30 mins)

- Coding (40 mins)

Coding questions were super direct and easy:

Q1: Find numbers between X and Y whose sum of digits is equal to the highest digit of the number. (E.g., 100: 1+0+0 = 1, and highest digit is also 1) Q2: Return the count of elements whose position changed after sorting and whose position remained same. (E.g., 2 1 3 4 → 1 2 3 4 → Count = 2, 2)

2. Technical Interview 1 [ 41 candidates were selected ]

Started with a quick intro exchange. The interviewer was chill and said he'll go through my resume while I solve a DSA question.

Before starting, he asked what data structures I'm familiar with. I mentioned stacks, queues, linked lists, graphs, hashmaps, and priority queues. I didn't mention trees on purpose, since I wasn't confident and didn't want a question from that topic.

Q1: LRU Cache (just the logic was enough) Q2: Reverse Linked List (this had to be coded live)

I clarified doubts and kept explaining my thought process. If you're stuck, talk it out, they guide you. (For the LRU question, I initially started with a solution that was quite far from the correct approach. The interviewer noticed this and helped guide me a bit. He then asked me to take some time to think it through. After that, I was able to figure out the correct and optimal solution.)

Then we moved on to resume and project discussions.

He gave me a solid tip:

"If you're giving results (Eg. reduced response time by 80%) in your projects, make sure they're real and not simulated."

Next came:

● Straightforward OOPs pillars

● REST API basics (since it was in my resume)

● Asked what is idempotency -- I blanked out and said so. He was chill about it.

● PUT vs PATCH -- discussed that too.

Wrapped up with me asking about automation in banking.

Tip: Stay calm even if you miss something. Don't panic. Just be honest and smile through it.

3. Technical Interview 2 [ 22 candidates were selected ]

Again, a friendly start. This time two interviewers were there.

I was asked about my strongest skills. I said DBMS, SQL, and Java.

He first asked the port numbers of MySQL and PostgreSQL, which I didn't know. Then:

● Sharding, partitioning, and database optimization.

● Write an SQL to count students with the same name grouped by year.

● A Java function to put(key, value) and get(key), twist was that value can be any type (int, string, etc. in the same map). You are allowed to use HashMap.

I tried many ways but couldn't crack that multi-type value part.

They were cross-questioning a lot -- not to grill, but to test confidence. Stick to your answer unless you're really wrong.

They also asked:

● About my projects

● How form data is stored in a DB the process flows.

● Something on database indexes and B-tree (I didn't know and said so)

● Asked about JWT tokens in depth.

The interview ended with me asking a question:

"How do you decide which new tech or feature to adopt?"

This round was more of a stress test not to check if you know everything, but to see how you stay calm under pressure, explain your thoughts clearly, and stick to your answers with confidence. They also wanted to see if you communicate clearly and can admit honestly when you don't know something, without losing confidence.

4. HR round [ 9 candidates were selected ]

This round felt more like a friendly chat than an interview. The HR was very calm and welcoming.

She started with simple questions like:

● "How was your day?"

● "Where do you stay?"

● "Tell me something not in your resume."

● "Apart from salary, what do you look for in a company?"

Then came some situational questions, like:

● "What would you do if ICICI gave you a job offer with the same pay?"

● "What if your teammate is not cooperating on a project?"

● "What would you do if your manager calls you out during a team meeting?"

● "What quality in a person irritates you the most?"

● "What if your manager has those traits that irritate you?"

● "How do you handle conflict or disagreement in a team?"

Tips: Keep your answers honest but aligned with company values. Also, prepare a few things that aren't in your resume -- hobbies, side projects, values, or personal traits. If you've made something that your family or friends actually use, make sure to mention it no matter how small . That usually gets them really interested.

5. Business Round (Not what it sounds like) [ 9 candidates were selected ]

This was taken by a Senior Executive from IDFC, and was completely online. Honestly, it was more of a casual conversation.

We started by introducing ourselves. He saw aviation as one of my hobbies, and we ended up talking about that quite a bit (which was fun ✈ ).

He then asked me about:

● My projects

● Some basic questions on what I worked on

That was it - very short and sweet (~15 mins). We wrapped up with me asking him about banking automation again.

The results were out the next day, and 8 candidates were selected.

Placement Process:

● The Placement process started with the announcement of the PPT (pre-placement talk) which was in the second last week of July. The dates of OA (online assessment) were announced shortly and were scheduled for the next week.

● A total of 4 interview rounds were conducted, excluding the online assessment. There were 2 technical rounds, 1 HR discussion round and the last Business round which turned out to be a technical and curriculum discussion round for me.
journey.prep:
● Start early with DSA and development. It gives you a very strong edge over others. You may think that you have a lot of time, indeed it is true, but do not underestimate the power of consistency and long time efforts. Most people do not start preparation until they have completed their 5th semester. I started in the 3rd semester with DSA and development in the 4th semester.

● Do not be stuck in the "Dev or DSA" hell. YOU MUST HAVE BOTH OF THEM AT A PRETTY GOOD LEVEL. Nowadays everybody knows the MERN stack and it has become the new normal, do not limit yourself to only one technology. Explore other technologies as well like Java Development, Spring boot, etc. Make some projects which actually solve real world problems, not just a CRUD application with some eye-catching UI which is made by vercel v0 or claude.

● Participate in hackathons and solve their problem statements, even if you cannot win the hackathon do not stop building the application for the problem. You will anyways have a solid project with you if you keep on working with the statement.

● Do not ignore system design. It is now becoming common to ask system design to freshers and may happen that it will become a part of your process like DSA. At least know the basics of HLD, LLD and have a knowledge about the famous questions of system design. Use Aryan Mittal for system design.

● Give leetcode/codeforces/codechef/atcoder contests, they help you keep your mind in the correct momentum which is needed during the placement season. You cannot stop your mind midway through the season. Having internships with proper firms gives you an edge, because nowadays everybody has some kind of internship experience. If you do not have an internship, then you have to work a little more to compete with the ones having internships. Do not get inferiority complex with the people who have summer internships or any other. Hard work and consistency makes a lot of difference.

● DO NOT EXPECT THE PLACEMENT SEASON TO BE VERY SMOOTH. You have to be mentally strong for this and rejections are a part of it. I messed up my PhonePe interview because I did not know a specific advanced DSA concept (Binary Lifting) which led to my rejection. Do not think that advanced topics are not required for freshers. You never know what is waiting for you.

● Do not follow just one DSA sheet. One sheet may have concepts which the other may not. Go with striver, babbar for DSA. For CS fundamentals use Babbar, Kunal Kushwaha for OOPS. Do competitive programming, use TLE eliminators for that. Use TLE post contest discussion, they usually have solutions of up to 4-5 problems. Even if you have a low rating, watch and solve the later problems as they involve some good concepts which can sometimes pop up in front of you, and your mind gets trained to handle tougher problems.

● Keep your CGPA good enough, at least try to keep it above 8, it will help you to sit for all the companies. Sometimes the outcome is not in your hands, you may not pass the OA even after completely solving all the questions (happened to me with Zeta). Just make peace with it and look for the next company. Don't give a second thought to what is in the past. Don't let it bother you.

● Keep working and you will make it where you deserve. Hard work can never go in vain. Do not fall into that hardwork vs smartwork and all that superficial stuff. Keep it simple and drag yourself through it. Do not jumble yourself in tutorial hell, how to give interviews, how to smartly approach a problem, bla bla bla. Just be you and practice hard.

You may contact me here: Linkedin Resume: Link

All the best.

● The Placement process started with the announcement of the PPT (pre-placement talk) which was in the second last week of July. The dates of OA (online assessment) were announced shortly and were scheduled for the next week.

● A total of 4 interview rounds were conducted, excluding the online assessment. There were 2 technical rounds, 1 HR discussion round and the last Business round which turned out to be a technical and curriculum discussion round for me.

● The placement process for IDFC is too hectic because of so many rounds and the rigorous nature of interviews. I would advise not to go lightly and do not hope for any chill interview rounds, the selection is also too strict and depends entirely on the first 2 technical rounds. The people who passed the technical interviews and appeared for the HR round were all selected except a few people which was really disheartening.

1. Online Assessment [ 135 candidates appeared for this round ]

● This round was conducted on the campus, it was around 1hr 15 minutes test. The criteria for this round was on the basis of branches. EXTC was not allowed to sit for the process and were informed almost 10-15 minutes prior to the OA.

● The test consisted of 3 sections, General aptitude, CS fundamentals, DSA

● In the aptitude section, normal aptitude questions like probability, profit loss, worker problem, speed and time were asked. There were around 15 questions and we were given 25 minutes to solve them. The aptitude test I felt was easy and was solvable (I hate aptitude and do not practice for it and just tend to skip them in the test if I could not get the idea by seeing the question (absolutely not recommended ❌❌❌)). For aptitude refer indiabix website, and practice quantitative and pattern recognition questions.

● The next section was on CS fundamentals. It included questions from DBMS, OS, CCN, OOPS. Basic questions were asked in this section, such that if you have a good knowledge of your syllabus from the 2nd year then you would be able to tackle this section fairly. You can refer to Babbar's youtube channel for DBMS, OS and Kunal Kushwaha for OOPS.

● The third section was DSA. The questions asked in this section were fairly straightforward and were solvable by any brute force idea. The problem with this section was with the different programming languages (ideally should not happen, but happened with Java and Python people). I did not have to think on this section as I directly implemented the solutions.

1. The first problem was that we needed to find the sum of good numbers from a range [l, r], a good number is a number in which the difference between the sum of all the digits in the number and the largest digit is exactly equal to the largest digit. Eg 3003 ((3+0+0+3)-3 == 3). The brute force idea worked but gave TLE in most languages like C++, Java. I implemented it in C and was able to pass all the test cases.

2. The second problem was to find out that after sorting an array how many elements did not change their position. Again a fairly simple problem and just using the inbuilt sort function worked, I did it in C++ and passed all the test cases. Again, it was a problem with Java and Python people with the input and test cases. For passing the online assessment, I recommend practicing aptitude and do not skip it like I did because solving aptitude along with DSA will help you get an edge over others. Do leetcode, codeforces, codechef or any other platform that you like, DO NOT skip over any advanced DSA topic however difficult it may seem (cost me my phonepe interview had I known lifting beforehand). Solving advanced DSA problems helps you build the instinct where you do not have to put efforts into coming up with a solution.

After this round around 45 candidates were selected. The mistakes in the DSA section were taken into account by the company and the students who wrote a correct solution were selected.

2. Technical Round 1 [ 45 candidates appeared for this round ]

● This round was conducted on campus on 30th July in the morning. There were 9 panels and each panel had 2 interviewers. This round mainly focused on the core CS knowledge of the candidates like basic data structures, OOPS, Schema Design, etc. The round lasted around 45-50 minutes.

● When I entered the room, they shook hands with me and told me to sit. They did not ask for my introduction (I was not asked to introduce myself in any interviews I gave (don't know the reason behind that)). They took a copy of my resume, took a look at it and then asked whether I am ready to start with the interview.

● They started with very very basic questions on data structures like what are the types of data structures (linear, non-linear), when to use which, what is stacks and queues, how will you implement stack using queues and vice-versa, what are linked lists and their types. They were very basic questions and if you have even the lowest level of knowledge then you should be able to answer their questions without hesitation. (I would suggest when you are definitely clear with the answer, make some stories and tell, do not tell directly, this allows you to cover time and list down some extra points in front of the interviewer which many candidates would not have mentioned had they been in a hurry.)

● Then he asked me about my primary programming language. I said I use C++ for problem solving, Javascript and Nodejs for I/O intensive developmental tasks and Java Springboot for CPU heavy developmental tasks. So they went ahead to ask about OOPS of C++ and Java. I

was told to explain every concept with respect to both of the languages and highlight the differences between them.

● He asked me about polymorphism, inheritance, the diamond problem of multiple inheritance and how it is handled in Java and C++, friend functions and classes with their counterparts in Java. When to use Java, when to use C++. He basically asked me the whole of OOPS, in about 25 minutes and I was able to answer all of the questions.

● Next he gave me a situation of an online shopping platform which will sell products of all the types like electronics, clothes, food and everything, basically Amazon. He asked me how I would design the schema of this platform and handle the categories of products. He asked me how I will make the foreign key relations, what kind of attributes I store and how many tables would I require.

● Then on this schema he asked me to find products of a particular category, a particular brand, and above a particular rating. He told me to write a query on that and I was able to write the query (it was a simple query of inner join with some where clauses).

● Next he asked me how I track the trends of the customers who visited the platform. To this I answered by keeping the search history, keywords, order details and similar preferences of the user in a vectorized form inside the database and using it to predict the preferences of the users. I went a bit into machine learning for this question and was able to tell them the flow on how we will gather the data of user behaviour and use it to suggest similar products to the customer to boost the business.

For the technical round, I would suggest having a strong knowledge of the CS fundamentals and programming languages on your finger tips. It is not an exaggeration, this is what makes a difference while giving the feedback. Be calm in the interview and answer every question to the point, by making some stories to sugarcoat your answer. If you absolutely know the answer to a question, cook the response as much as you can, do not give straightforward answers like some AI or a robot. Keep your theory knowledge crisp with reasons for every fact, you need to know what is happening and why something is made in a certain way.

After this round around 22 candidates were shortlisted for the next round

3. Technical Round 2 [ 22 candidates appeared for this round ]

● This round was conducted on campus on 30th July. There were 6 panels and each panel had 2 interviewers. This round focused on core development knowledge, system design and problem solving. This round lasted around 45 minutes and was fast paced. We were expected to answer quickly like a rapid fire round, the interviewer did not show any kind of expression from which students could make out whether they were satisfied with the answer or not.

● They started by asking me about my day, I told them it was going fine uptill now. Then they proceeded to test my developmental knowledge by asking deep questions like what is actually nodejs and why it was developed. Then they proceeded to ask some system design questions like how would you scale a system if a lot of users came to your application. They did not even listen to the full answer, interrupted between every question and changed to the

next question abruptly. This would have been a tactic to test the candidate in difficult situations and how they would react under pressure.

● I heard from other candidates that they were taunting the students like "you fumbled here how would you handle in IDFC" or "you have mentioned so and so technology on your resume then you should be aware of it".

● They then proceeded to ask me a DSA question, only my panel was asking DSA. The problem required me to find the longest palindromic substring in a given string. The problem could be found on leetcode (5th problem on leetcode). They told me I have 15 minutes to code for the solution. The panelist handed me their macbook and told me to write the code on an online compiler. I had to write in codeforces style i.e. taking the input and then printing the longest palindromic substring. They did not care about the most optimal approach or the time and space complexity. They just wanted a working code and also did not provide any details about the question like constraints and all. After coding they asked me to explain the approach I took. It was a fairly simple problem and I was able to solve it in about 10 minutes. Thinking out loud, or explaining while coding was not at all required, their sole purpose was to get a working code.

● After this they tried to run the code but the online compiler was not working due to some internet issues. In spite of this they told me that my code is incorrect and has errors that is why it was not working. I argued with them that the code I wrote could not be incorrect and made them try running the code meanwhile the other interviewer went on to ask further questions.

● He asked me a puzzle. I have coins of denominations {1,2,5} and had to make a sum by taking at least one coin from every denomination. There was no logic involved in this puzzle and I just had to mod the sum by every denomination. While I was answering this the other interviewer finally ran the code by installing a GCC compiler on his macbook and accepted that the code was working perfectly. This gave me an edge as the other candidates in my panel faced a similar issue of the online compiler not working. Be prepared to face tougher situations as the purpose of further rounds is to test how mentally strong you are. DO NOT MELT IN FRONT OF THE INTERVIEWER HOWEVER RUDE OR UNINTERESTED THEY MAY SEEM. If the interviewer interrupts you in between, take it as a positive point because you were already on the right track and they got it, that is why they change the questions. Have confidence in yourself and do not underestimate yourself, if you are sure of something then do argue with the interviewer, sometimes they are also at fault.

After this 9 candidates were selected for the HR round.

4. HR Round [ 9 candidates appeared for this round ]

● The HR round was pretty chill. She was taking around 45 minute interviews of the candidates but due to time constraints (it was past 6 in the evening), she took the remaining candidates' interviews for about 15-20 minutes each.

● She started by asking how my day was, when I came to college for the interviews and how was the interview process in general. She asked where I stay and asked what my parents do.

● She asked me pretty straightforward behavioral and situational questions. She started by asking what if the manager is out of reach and does not reply, what will you do. Then she asked what if the manager micro-manages you, what will you do in this scenario.

● She also asked what would be my melting point (the point where you feel you will leave the company). All the questions were pretty standard, and I used pretty standard answers that chatGPT gives when we ask it to prepare for the HR round.

● The candidates who got shortlisted for the HR round were most probably guaranteed of the job, so the HR round was not very serious. The HR lady on the outside told us not to worry, they will try their best not to reject anyone after this. Prepare for the HR round by chatGPT. They ask pretty standard questions and you are expected to give their standard answers as well, like a viva. Try to stay calm and smile in front of the HR

All 9 candidates appeared for the next round.

5. Business Round [ 9 candidates appeared for this round ]

● This round was like a mere formality in the beginning as we have come a long way in clearing three intense interviews throughout the day. The interview was about 30 minutes and this was conducted in online mode because it was too late in the evening. Initially it was planned to take this round for half of the candidates on the next day, but we insisted to the HR lady (she was very friendly) to take it and complete it today itself, and they did so.

● Initially we were completely unaware as to what will be asked in this round as the HR also did not have any idea about the business round. She told us it may be related to the college curriculum that we have studied till now or something like that.

● The round for me turned out to be another technical round. The interviewer first asked me about my favorite subjects in college to which I answered DBMS, OS, Distributed Computing. So he began asking about DC. He asked me about system scalability, design patterns and concurrency in the case of distributed systems. I was well versed with DC in my sem 6 so I was able to answer all the questions pretty easily.

● He then asked me the difference between frontend and backend (I don't know why such a question), so based on my answer he started cross questioning me about the difference between UI/UX and some other jargon. I was able to answer all the questions but felt that the interview didn't go as intended. Be ready for surprises as this round was not initially planned. IDFC is known to have many interview rounds before selecting the candidates. Also do not assume that if you have come this far then it is absolutely guaranteed that you will get selected, as one candidate was not selected after these 4 rigorous interview rounds. I don't know the reason for that but it was pretty unfortunate.

Finally 8 candidates were finally selected for IDFC.

customSections.title: Advice & Tips for Juniors
customSections.content:
● Start early with DSA and development. It gives you a very strong edge over others. You may think that you have a lot of time, indeed it is true, but do not underestimate the power of consistency and long time efforts. Most people do not start preparation until they have completed their 5th semester. I started in the 3rd semester with DSA and development in the 4th semester.

● Do not be stuck in the "Dev or DSA" hell. YOU MUST HAVE BOTH OF THEM AT A PRETTY GOOD LEVEL. Nowadays everybody knows the MERN stack and it has become the new normal, do not limit yourself to only one technology. Explore other technologies as well like Java Development, Spring boot, etc. Make some projects which actually solve real world problems, not just a CRUD application with some eye-catching UI which is made by vercel v0 or claude.

● Participate in hackathons and solve their problem statements, even if you cannot win the hackathon do not stop building the application for the problem. You will anyways have a solid project with you if you keep on working with the statement.

● Do not ignore system design. It is now becoming common to ask system design to freshers and may happen that it will become a part of your process like DSA. At least know the basics of HLD, LLD and have a knowledge about the famous questions of system design. Use Aryan Mittal for system design.

● Give leetcode/codeforces/codechef/atcoder contests, they help you keep your mind in the correct momentum which is needed during the placement season. You cannot stop your mind midway through the season. Having internships with proper firms gives you an edge, because nowadays everybody has some kind of internship experience. If you do not have an internship, then you have to work a little more to compete with the ones having internships. Do not get inferiority complex with the people who have summer internships or any other. Hard work and consistency makes a lot of difference.

● DO NOT EXPECT THE PLACEMENT SEASON TO BE VERY SMOOTH. You have to be mentally strong for this and rejections are a part of it. I messed up my PhonePe interview because I did not know a specific advanced DSA concept (Binary Lifting) which led to my rejection. Do not think that advanced topics are not required for freshers. You never know what is waiting for you.

● Do not follow just one DSA sheet. One sheet may have concepts which the other may not. Go with striver, babbar for DSA. For CS fundamentals use Babbar, Kunal Kushwaha for OOPS.

journey.projects: Core projects and domain architectures discussed in interview rounds.
journey.howSecured:
Online Assessment: this was the first round which consisted of 3 sections

1. general aptitude / reasoning - 20 min

2. Core cs fundamentals - 30 min

3. Coding Section - 40 min

Core cs fundamentals involved mcqs based on code snippets/flowcharts, DBMS, OS, SQL. It was completely language independent and basic level questions were asked.

Coding section involved two easy questions-

1. Given an array of integers, return the count of correctly placed and incorrectly placed integers if the array was sorted. It was quite easy and the attached problem is almost similar to it. (link)

2. Given 2 integers that represent a range from x to y, find the sum of all the golden numbers where a golden number is defined as a number whose sum of digits - maximum digit is equal to maximum digit (eg- 352: 3 + 5 + 2 = 10, max digit = 5, so 10-5 = 5 ie sum-maxd = maxd). I was not able to pass all the test cases idk if there was some issue with setting the testcase (did 7/10). This was the crux but the question was in a story format like we encounter over codeforces(so better if you are already familiar with that type)

TIPS:

● Time management is very important in the first 2 sections. Questions are doable but the decision to attempt or skip a particular question based upon time is more important.

● Many python users faced issues in this round and this was seen in PhonePe as well, so if you've enough time consider shifting to cpp/java

1. Technical Round 1 [ 37 candidates appeared for this round ]

This round was entirely about the basics of OOP and core subjects (OS and CCN) and schema design. It started with a short introduction followed by OOP fundamentals in your first language, mine was cpp so in depth questions related to friend functions/virtual keyword/multiple inheritance/destructors were asked followed by some questions related to OS and CCN. I was also asked about the basics of Cloud computing even though I didn't have any project related to it. So in this case answer honestly whatever you know and try to relate concepts.

Later the interviewer asked me to design a schema for an e-commerce platform, followed by how would you design a recommendation system over this and how would you store overhead data specifically in which tables. I was then asked to write a basic SQL query over these tables using 2 joins. This was extended into a discussion related to system design: how would you scale this, what databases will you use(sql/nosql/both with reasoning) and how would you prevent bruteforce attacks(IP blacklisting using Redis). This round went on for about 35-40 mins.

TIPS:

● Make sure you are clear with the basics of your first language and have some idea of OOP in Java too if java isn't your first language. Also never ignore OOP in your first language, even though you've mastered it in Java, have a basic understanding of how that works in your preferred language.

● Also from what I got to know, candidates who had their first language as Java, were also asked about development in Java (Springboot related) so be prepared to handle such situations.

● Design problems are to check how you approach a problem so take your time and think in 360 degree just to not miss out on any part. Make sure you ask genuine questions related to company tech at the end.

2. Technical Round 2 [ 22 candidates appeared for this round ]

This round was focused more towards resume and Low Level Design(LLD). After introduction I was drilled down on a single project where they even asked me how do you write config files, how do you build docker images and configure kubernetes and everything, so make sure you do projects yourself as they also check github in some cases. They also asked what all types of databases you've worked on apart from mongoDB and Mysql and what are their use cases(vector db and key value pair db like redis)

In the later part I was asked to give a low level design of a cab booking system (Ola/Uber). So in LLD, they expect you to use OOP and data structures and algorithms and I was asked to write code structure in cpp (classes, functions they will have, what each func will do and which data structure and algo it will use). Keep discussing with the interviewer what all things you are considering, like at the first step I asked if I had to design for both drivers and passengers so he said no continue only with passengers.

So I went on to do it that way and told them that Dijkstra's would be required but I won't simply apply it over all the drivers. I will set a radius range r initially small(lets say 500m) and if I found drivers within that range they would be sent to client side(passenger) and if not found the radius wound be increased to say 1km and the process would go on until a driver is encountered or we exceed the max radius which can be set to 5km. Along with this, I would also use a priority queue to keep track of "k" nearest drives in case the first one rejects or something(they see how you handle edge cases). I also mentioned that we would need to

implement a lock in a way so that 2 passengers don't book the same cab for diff destinations and explained how that part would be implemented in the driver part of the design. Then they asked follow up questions like what if multiple passengers are requesting the same driver then which passenger would be allocated to the driver (which actually happens in the real world). We kept discussing and enhancing the system and this round went on for 30 min or so.

TIPS:

● Yes surprisingly most of us were never asked about DSA problems.

● For all your projects make a google doc with all the important points/features, their implementation and tech stack as it becomes really easy to revise the entire project cause at the last moment we feel we need to revise everything.

● Also add to it what problems did you faced and how did you resolve them as it is a check question if you've done the project yourself or not

● Whenever you feel confused, communicate with the interviewer, they'll surely help you out. It's okay even if you ask them if you're doing right or not so they can guide you well to produce a solution.

3. HR Round [ 9 candidates who appeared for this round ]

It was a classic HR round, more of a conversation type where I was asked some basic questions like why do you want to join IDFC and all. I was given situations and was asked how would you resolve this. Here mainly they check if the candidate is culturally fit and would be able to coordinate with the team so just keep a good smile and try to connect answers to your own experiences. Mention about the ppt/research that you do which adds more weightage to your answer.

I was asked the following questions-

1. What one thing could piss you off at work?

2. How would you deal with a team mate who is not coordinating/communicating?

3. If you're a manager and supposed to give a best team member award, what criteria would you consider before deciding the winner apart from tech/development?

TIPS:

● Try to connect answers with company values. Read about their vision/mission, tagline, history, this really helps in HR based rounds.

● There might be some trick questions which play on our psychology so it is always safer to answer honestly.

● Be friendly with the interviewer and reflect your true personality.

4. Online Screening Round [ 9 candidates who appeared for this round ]

It was an extra round conducted online which started at 8:30pm. It was just a fitment round where I was asked to explain my projects to a very senior positioned interviewer which lasted for just 15 mins. There

I was directly asked to send the repo link of my project and explain it. Keep in mind don't take such a round lightly as elimination does take place here which unfortunately did happen for one of my peers. Some candidates were asked about the subjects in previous semester or the course work, so make sure you have an idea of that as well, they don't expect details but just the list of subjects and topics that you've learned.

The results were declared the next day and 8 students received the offer.

So i know the placement season is a very hectic and tiring period but dont give up this was my third interview before this i didnt even pass few of the OAs and had also felt really disheartened when i got rejected in MSCI since it was one the company i had aimed for and dont end up taking a company that you had never wished for since i am sure you might end up regretting later, atleast in the start there might be few companies that is very

3. Be well versed with your intro and the question to be asked be ready with that try to match it with your interest or the companies tech related, i always asked some question that was AI related or some projects where they were including AI or something like that so be prepared for that as well.

4. Whatever i had learnt i initially didnt make notes be it for my DSA or SQL or anything keep it ready so as soon as a company comes you then give time to prepare for researching about the company or anything extra you might need for preparing and not wasting on learning something which you had already did before.

5. And for internship here i was able to give a reason but it might not be acceptable for many people i thought if its unpaid then i might not get to learn anything its not true, but for that sake dont even pay for those fake internship there you get to do only those projects which are available on the youtube you get no industrial level experience

6. Before your interview dont keep on mugging up things coz when you try to learn in the last moment you end up messing other things which you would be well versed with, so calm down listen to some music and just revise whatever you have learnt so far.

7. And mainly i repeat dont get sad because you couldnt clear the interview ofc there you should have strong fundamentals but it also depends on luck too the only thing in your hand is to clear the OA the rest of the things you cant predict what happens next.

journey.projects: Core projects and domain architectures discussed in interview rounds.
journey.howSecured:
The company first conducted a pre-placement talk, which was followed by an online assessment few days later. After that 4 interview rounds were conducted on 30th July.

1. Online Assesment [ 135 students appeared for it]

This was conducted on the HirePro platform & duration was for 75mins. The test consisted of 3 sections, each with a time limit. The first section had 15 questions and was aptitude based wherein general questions on logical reasoning were asked. The second section had 25 technical questions based on Excel, CCN, OS, OOPs and Basic Statistics. The third section had 2 coding questions which were quite easy.

- Q1) How many elements are correctly sorted. Correct place means Rightly indexed when seen from a Sorted perspective. Ex: 1 3 2 4 5 sorted is 1 2 3 4 5 1 and 4 are in the correct place , whereas 3 and 2 are not in the correct place. So the result would be 2, 3 Since 2 are incorrect and 3 are correct

- Q2) Had to find the number of golden number in a given range where the golden number meant the sum of the digits of a number - max number = max number Ex: 325 is a golden number (3+2+5) - 5 = 5

2. Technical Round 1 [ 41 students appeared ]

Initially 47 to 50 students were there but then many got selected in barclays so finally 41 students had appeared for this round. This round lasted for me around 45 mins to 1hr. I was the 1st person that was to be interviewed in my panel. It started with my introduction and then he directly jumped into a DSA problem it was related to cache so we had a buffer size of N and whenever we pushed an element it had a certain TTL (time_to_live) so

suppose an element entered the buffer at 10:20 and its TTL was 2mins then at 10:23 it was supposed to be popped out of the cache and make room for other elements to enter. Initially i started with a hashmap solution but as soon as i started explaining i got the Priority Queue solution using heap here since my primary language was python he was checking my syntax or the function that i was mentioning with GFG and since in GFG the priority queue implementation was not the one using heap he started asking what is heap, heapify and balanced binary tree which i was able to explain it all.

Then he started grilling me on GenAI and bit of ML since my entire resume was based on that Q1) Difference between GenAI and unsupervised learning (Generates new content and solely revolves around the input to find structure) Q2) What is the output of unsupervised learning models (Clusters, Dimensionality Reduction) Q3) Architecture of GenAI (Input layer + Tokenization + Embedding + Transformer + Attention Mechanism+ Decoder/output generator) Here i gave a brief overview of each layer and was trying to keep it as detailed as possible since i didnt want him to ask any more question in depth over here since i hadnt done transformers architecture in detail. Q4) How does its matches the user context and generates an appropriate content (Semantic Similarity) Q4) What is RAG Q5) In a glimpse explain what is prompt engineering Q6) Since i had explained RAG with the example of a medical chatbot he asked if a user prompts and says he cant concentrate in his work but the bot doesn't have any idea, as concentrate is not there in its DB then what will i do to give a proper response, initially i had said if at any point the bot cannot give a proper advice then i would have a default response wherein it will provide a general physician and he can take his concern forward with him but this wasn't what he had expected he said that the chatbot should ask few more questions on what he i feeling so that he can reach a conclusion and then provide a solution

He did ask few more questions based on AIML which i am not able to recollect but then it ended with me asking a question based on AIs usage in IDFC and one common question

3. Technical Round 2 [ 22 students]

This round lasted for around 40 mins for me

Here i didnt even feel i would get selected as the people who had went previous to me were all coming out demotivated since they were asked questions based on system design, AWS, CCN and i hadnt prepared in that terms at all but i was lucky since i was not asked such Qs

DSA : Valid Parenthesis Resume Based:

1. Asked me to explain one of my data analytics project it was dashboard based then asked few questions based on that

2. Since I had SQL in my resume they asked me what kind of projects I have done. I explained one, then they asked few simple queries based on the project explained, they were based on aggregate, group by and one subquery related cant remember the exact questions but all of them was very easy.

3. What is Jupyter Notebook and why use it when you have PyCharm or other IDEs

4. Then they asked which OS did i use since OS was mentioned in my resume (I had said windows on my personal laptop and it was ubuntu on college PC) so they started asking some linux commands and more related to that

5. Since my primary language was python they asked few questions based on that like types of exception handling in python and revolved around that more

6. Then they gave me a usecase kinda question like suppose there would be finger scanner for storing many peoples data what all would be your approaches. This was kind of an open ended question they wanted to see my how i would approach it (Here i would say ask whatever question you can possibly ask, coz more than the answer they want to see what you think so i asked what kind of data will be stored they said 0s and 1s i instantly started thinking in terms of FOSIP though i couldnt think much but mentioned few of the things that i could remember like grayscaling image optimization, thresholding and RLE and as i kept answering i even asked do we need to even process on the storage part for that they said you may so i mentioned a bit about the server and load balancing since they had said millions of data will be there and so on to retrieve as and when needed so but this a gist there was a detailed conversation on this) There were few more questions but were based on fundamentals and were answerable and in the ending asked the same question as before.

4. HR [ 9 students]

This round for me was only for around 20 mins since it was getting really late they had to finish it and take another round online but for starting 3 or 2 people they took it for almost 1 hr.

Unlike other rounds this wasnt that restrictive it was pretty much chill and the HR was also kind and friendly She started by asking me to introduce myself without any tech aspect and anything which is not there in my resume (So here i would say try speaking something which would be cool and might impress them so i spoke about my part in my schools kho kho team and about my bharatnatyam career) Then asked Various questions like

1. Being a women if your idea didnt reach the higher management what would you do

2. Have you ever reached a meltingPoint, if yes then how did you deal with it

3. Why did you take CSE-AIML

4. A policy that you would want to be made compulsory by the company for all the women working

5. In 5 or 10 years where do you see yourself There were few more women based situationship based question (try being as diplomatic as you can)

4. Technical [ 9 students]

So they decided to take another round online and this was again pretty much chill Questions included are:

1. Introduce yourself

customSections.content:
So i know the placement season is a very hectic and tiring period but dont give up this was my third interview before this i didnt even pass few of the OAs and had also felt really disheartened when i got rejected in MSCI since it was one the company i had aimed for and dont end up taking a company that you had never wished for since i am sure you might end up regretting later, atleast in the start there might be few companies that is very

1. In all your interviewees keep on asking their name coz though it didnt happen for me but for few they had asked who had interviewed them before

2. Be at your best behaviour and without realizing we end up doing those faces, like whenever we dont know an answer or even when we are definitely sure of an answer coz they do judge on basis of everything so keep a control on that as well.

3. Be well versed with your intro and the question to be asked be ready with that try to match it with your interest or the companies tech related, i always asked some question that was AI related or some projects where they were including AI or something like that so be prepared for that as well.

4. Whatever i had learnt i initially didnt make notes be it for my DSA or SQL or anything keep it ready so as soon as a company comes you then give time to prepare for researching about the company or anything extra you might need for preparing and not wasting on learning something which you had already did before.

5. And for internship here i was able to give a reason but it might not be acceptable for many people i thought if its unpaid then i might not get to learn anything its not true, but for that sake dont even pay for those fake internship there you get to do only those projects which are available on the youtube you get no industrial level experience

6. Before your interview dont keep on mugging up things coz when you try to learn in the last moment you end up messing other things which you would be well versed with, so calm down listen to some music and just revise whatever you have learnt so far.

7. And mainly i repeat dont get sad because you couldnt clear the interview ofc there you should have strong fundamentals but it also depends on luck too the only thing in your hand is to clear the OA the rest of the things you cant predict what happens next.

8. Keep practicing don't let your one failure mess up your other possible victory.

[ List down the rounds that were conducted and any specific information related to it ]

1. [Online Assessment] [ Around 140 candidates ][28th July]

The OA consisted of 3 Sections,Logical reasoning(20 minutes),Aptitude(20 minutes) and DSA Questions (40 mins-2 questions).Each question was shut after that allotted time so make sure to read all instructions carefully, so you can attempt all questions. The MCQ's weren't from a specific section , you had to have knowledge about various sections like OOPS,SQL,Basics of development etc, aptitude solving, so there is no separate thing you could do for this section, its striking in the moment and some basic knowledge that you gathered over the years. No amount of mcq study could guarantee marks in this section, just answer the ones you are sure about and do a guess on others as there was not any negative marking.

Coming to the DSA section- there were 2 DSA questions, both were quite easy, the first was about sorting , the other one I don't remember the exact question but if you are able to solve Leetcode easy-medium section, this will be a cakewalk. I was able to pass all test cases for the first question, but left 3 test cases for the second one which was a case for almost every student , so relatively it was all the same , hardly anyone solved the entire question. So it's about you trying every solution, even brute force, that comes to your mind because you never know that's what everyone did.

2. [Technical Interview 1] [ 45 candidates shortlisted][30th July,2025]

There were 2 interviewers on the panel, so don't get intimidated.The interview began with "Tell me about yourself", you actually don't need immense prep for this one, just give them a basic overview of what all you did in college years(like DSA,dev,internship(if any),extracurricular activities) , I feel that's enough.Now this interview wasn't in any flow, they asked questions from all domains.

1.Basic Questions- Difference between Authentication and Authorization- I answered that followed by which they gave a scenario, there is a case wherein you have three sections , principle's cabin, teacher's cabin and the tpo office, everyone has an admin for that room, and a normal student who doesn't belong to any section needs access to one of these rooms(To clarify the instructions and problem definition wasn't as clear as I have mentioned here but over the discussion you kinda figure out the problem, so you need to DISCUSS with the panel about what you are thinking and if it matches with what they want an answer for, then proceed further, this tells them that you have a good habit of understanding problem statement clearly then moving to solution rather than just jumping without clear understanding). Initially I thought it was about jwt authorization but later I came to the conclusion that it had api keys involved and you had to give a token to everyone who requested it with an expiry time.-There is no certain prep you can do for these types of questions your dev concepts need to be clear which just comes by making projects.

2.OOPS- I was asked about multiple inheritance, the diamond problem I explained along with it, then about Private constructors(Singleton classes) and how they are called(getInstance method),abstraction,C++ vs Java(multiple inheritance,pointers,virtual inheritance).

3.Projects- Asked about how I implemented user authentication using Firebase(to which I gave a detailed explanation), why mongodb(explain abt sql vs no sql) db , why react(virtual dom etc),about use of api in projects.

4. I was asked for the system design of a URL shortener, to which I gave a rough answer(data structure to be used and flow of it).

3. [Technical Round 2] [22 candidates][30th July]

In this round with 2 interviewers again,it began with intro, then i was asked about

1. New vs malloc(keyword in java and c++), which is faster, which is better to which i wasn't really correct in all answers,to which the interviewer also said, "its visible , you aren't aware".

2. Then he asked about destructors and copy constructors, though I had read about them , due to his statement I just forgot about it.

At such points it's really important to keep your calm and look forward to points where you can show him your strengths.

3. Later I was asked a question to check if 4181 belongs to the fibonacci series(not normal fibonacci series printing) to which after some hints i was able to solve. For such non-traditional questions just keep thinking about different approaches and keep telling the interviewer, till he doesn't tell you to stop.

4. Later it came to some OOPS concepts again which were easy only, they did tell me to write pseudo code so even if your first language isnt java have a basic understanding of how to write classes and instantiate objects, and various keywords,they do tell you to write code.

5. Then came to my projects, and asked about various keywords, like JWT Auth,API's, DB storage, at such points its really important,that you explain them the motive behind each of your project and explain them key parts in detail, they just want to know that it's your original work that you created and with a purpose(is what the interviewer told me as a feedback.)

6. I was given a scenario about a project scaling and was given different scenarios and had to design schema for all of them and also write sql queries.

4. [HR Round] [9 candidates][28th July]

Initially it was for an hour, but later, due to time constraints it was for 20-25 minutes.Just be yourself in this interview they want to see the real you and align yourself with the company policies and motives. Also explain how you fit in the company giving real life examples. To be honest I didn't prepare anything for this round, just knew the policy(Always You First) and some motives(like ethics,etc).Take a few minutes to think,it gives you a lot many examples to speak about.

5. [Fitment/Tech round] [9 candidates ][28th July]

This one started at around 9:30 p.m. , we were at college from 8 a.m , be ready for such long days, and keep your mind prepared to answer equally well in such scenarios.I just left the hr round seconds within i was called for the next round, which was really quick.

This was about my favourite subjects I studied in the curriculum, then I made a mess here by saying soft computing(neural networks) which I had not revised after 4th sem. Then he ended up asking the difference between neural networks and machine learning, which set me a slight back, but took a pause of relief and thought , in basic

terms so i started with ml then recalled some of neural networks and finished the answers. Later he asked for an overview of all projects and this interview ended.

Results were declared next day and

[ 8 students were offered the job ]...

It's really important to study as per the interview experience , that guides you which topics are the most important for that company.Know your resume in and out and everything mentioned on it in detail, because that's the only piece of information they have about you, its ok to have less skills on resume but know everything in detail rather than having more and not knowing some.
