journey.howSecured:
1. [Online Assessment] [ 135+ Students were shortlisted ]

The OA had a few sections: Logical Aptitude, Technical Questions, and a final DSA section. Each section had its own timer. It's all about being choosy and smart enough to identify which questions are the low-hanging fruit for you.

Aptitude Section:---> Following is just the tentative vague description and not the exact question (I really can't remember the exact questions , but this description will really help you get a clear idea)

1)Coding-Decoding Analogy: If "FADE" is "GBWR" then follow the same pattern for some "xyzw" type of string 2)Number Theory: how many pairs(a,b) are there wherein division of a/b is not an integer {1,2,3,4…16} something like this. 3)Logical Reasoning Passage:A big 3-4 questions passage (Some 6 people , given word-equations(ratio etc) of relations of their savings and salaries) and then follow up questions (easy but time consuming) 4)Statistics: Mean , Variance , Standard deviation , Coefficient of Variation type of questions.(Mean of 10 students is 3 , but then some student has mark correction and then find new mean) 5)Basic Probability types question (12 box , 3 has trap , so P(no trap)) 6)Question like how many pair of letters are there for "HERITAGE" having as many letters as there in english alphabet series (something like this) 7)Profit % types question 8)Pipe-work time types question

Technical Section:---> 1)Proper Loops (do-while etc) as a figure , and then interpret the figure and tell how many times is the code running.

2) Some oops (basic) questions

3) Standard OS,CCN,DBMS,SQL questions 4)Port , Ping , Router , Queues , Quick sort , static keyword numerical , pointers numerical int arr[]= {10,20,30,40,50,60,70} then something like int *r=arr…. *r1=arr+2 …. *r2= arr+5… and then cout<< something related with r1, r2 etc

5) Binary search tree array ={4,1,2,16,8,33,62,76} something like this , what is left child of root. 6)Queue <int> of size 4, some position of front , rear pointers , removing 3 elements , and then MCQ based on the state of the queue. 7)2D matrix figure based manipulation question (flowchart based) 8)Mysql type question (easy)

9) OOPS (conceptual easy question) of inheritance , output based , etc 10)One crazy question about OS of CISCO organization for switches 11)Basic data structure type question (medium gate level question) : output based 12)How many times the flowchart's loop is running.

Coding question:--->

1) How many elements are there which are in the correct place and not in the correct place. Correct place means Rightly indexed when seen from a Sorted perspective. (easy isn't it?) ex: 1 3 2 4 sorted is 1 2 3 4 1 and 4 are in the correct place , whereas 3 and 2 are not in the correct place.

2) Given int x, int y and then count special numbers from x and y. Special number means SUM(DIGITS) == 2*(highest digit). Easy??

Points to ponder:--->

1) Be calm

2) Manage time smartly

3) Attack on low-hanging fruits first

4) Attempt questions which you are familiar first

5) Learn to leave lengthy questions

6) Don't get zoned out , every 1 minute has the same value :)

2. [Technical Round 1] [41 candidates ] (70-90 mins++) {Taken by 2 interviewers}

1) Introduce yourself

2) Was asked question on my projects

3) Specify about Skills , Tech Stack that you have practiced

4) DSA Question (Revolving around Bellman-ford algorithm)

5) What is a cloud? Proxy Server?

6) SQL vs Mongodb , which I have used in the project ? Why? Why not?

7) Real word Application for Abstraction , Stack , Queue and Tree and Graph

8) Port number of Mysql

9) Heavy discussion on my projects (AIML based) (Maths behind Random Forest , Logistic Regression) . Focus on Pipelines and Flow of building an ML Model (decide , Train , test , tune etc etc)

10) It is impressive if you have published some research paper (or it is in under progress)

11) Indexing in Databases

12) Varchar in SQL , why varchar ? How to change the Varchar (LENGTH) once the table is already created.

13) Triggers in SQL

14) Library in Python which I have used (numpy , nltk , pandas , sci-kit ,openCV)

15) Docker ? Kubernetes (I didn't know Kubernetes Technicality)

16) Was Asked about my approach to the latest DSA problem which I had solved (it was about Trie with Bits and finding the Maximum XOR )

17) Final question for the interviewer? : I asked : how was my interviewer and where am i lacking , they said it is important that as a developer , we must have some knowledge about cloud , how to deploy , some advanced real life usage of networking(ccn) , code to be written not just for localhost , but a scalable code for development+deployment etc.

Mind it:--->

1) Never give up while giving interview

2) Even if you don't know, try to struggle with the question , tell the interviewers about your perspective, they are really interested more on how you think about approaching a problem , if you succeed in this way then this is really impressive

3) Sometimes you may even get a question that "hey AIML project is all about templates etc ", that's where you must say that while making a project it is also about proper lifecycle of development and building model , which task? Which model? Why this? Why not that etc ?

4) Never say anything negative , it may backfire you during the interview.

5) Don't break down,if your interviewer is an expert in a field like (cloud computing) and you have zero idea on that field , just be real-self.

3. [Technical Round 2] [22 candidates ] (90-100 mins++) {Taken by 2 interviewers}

1) Introduce yourself

2) One DSA code to be written on an online compiler. Mine was an easy question: Find peak element in an (increasing and then decreasing type) of array (Binary search) , just ask a clarifying question , what if n==1?==2? and then what if len(decreasing part)==0?

3) Indexing in Database (but advanced level)

4) SQL query optimization, I was asked to first tell Select * from table with name like "T%" and then to optimize this query. (even if you don't know , just try to deliver a valid logic)

5) Again Applicability for all projects, WHY this ? WHY not that?

6) OOPS: Compile-time and run-time polymorphism (overloading , overriding ,constructor , public , private , inheritance , Abstraction , encapsulation ) All these in real-life

7) LLD design for Bank system , make classes , interfaces , controller(if you don't know , then study it beforehand) , methods , etc , clean code for RBI class (parent class) and then subclasses like IDFC bank , SBI bank etc , and each having some rules, compliance rules, seniorcitizen_Age etc , revolving around inheritance etc.

8) What happens when you type a message in whatsapp to your friend? what happens when you click on "send message" button.

9) How do you think messages travel from your phone to your friends phone? Protocols, headers , packets , trivial CCN stuff.

10) What are keys , why keys , normalization , MongoDB familiarity?

11) Code for Trigger (After Insert) , just insert the curTime in logs

12) Was asked about familiarity with Stored Procedures

13) Asked about HSS-Psychology course

14) Was asked about Data analytics and my QGIS findings of land cover change

15) Was asked about my (Airavat,Flipkart grid) Hackathon experience , projects etc

16) Final question for interviewers? I asked : Is there any way to do "Online transactions on mobile for metro between Ghatkopar and Azad Nagar without Internet" , then we had a healthy discussion for about 5+ minutes on this topic.

4. [HR Round] [9 Candidates] (20 mins++)

This was a fairly relaxed round, and the HR representative was very friendly and made me feel comfortable. The conversation included the following questions:

1) Something cool about me which I have not written on resume (I told about my love for chess)

2) Why do you want to join IDFC bank ? (Reality: Along with coding , I could know about ITR, finance , economics , equity , IPO , banking sector etc.)

3) Dream company apart from IDFC bank? (I told about my love for space , stars and ISRO)

4) How do you deal with rejections (on-campus 8 times )?

5) What if I wasn't selected today also? (Grind for the best opportunity)

6) Any creative Application ideas for HR? (I first bulleted the answer but she told me to think again and come up with a brilliant idea, so i presented my idea for emotion-detection-AI powered priority wise scheduler chatbot / employee-HR relation management site with color coding feature ). She was really impressed by this idea thought in a shorter timespan. Like she told me such an application is being used by her and that this idea was amazing.

7) Where do I live ? What do I do in my travel time to college?

8) Some behavioral question and that's it

9) Any final question for her :- I asked her about the Location for internship and then placement, She told that bootcamp may be in Banglore and then Joining for placement maybe in Mumbai.(most likely)

5. [Business Round] [9 Candidates ] (20-30 mins++){Taken by 1 interviewer}

Okay so I was pretty sure that yes I had made it to the end , and then we got to know that there is one more Technical Round with the senior engineers or VP or architects of the company.

It was an online round on Teams. I would recommend you to give it from college only , because there you will have support from college , TPO office , supportive TPCs (yes they really work hard for our placement for that entire day+night) ,Wifi , HRs etc. So even if there is some wifi problem or technical issue , they are there to handle it (SO GIVE IT FROM COLLEGE ONLY !!!)

1) Hey Tushar , Introduce yourself

2) Seen my resume (Screen shared)

3) Talked about my skills

4) Discussed about my projects (the one with the most impact driven cause to be discussed along with full flow , architecture , why this and why not that , the mathematics behind this-that , the impact it is having)

5) My interviewer was a senior architect. He was really very chill and made me feel comfortable even after facing some technical issues (wifi problem at 8:05 pm).

6) Final questions for him? :- I told him that I had presented my views(Technical round 2) on "online transactions on mobile without internet" and what his opinion was on this point. He praised this idea and said some work is going on by RBI and all banks and that there is a good scope in this field.

After appearing for almost 9 companies, cracking OAs , failing in some Round 1, sometimes Round 2 , Sometimes even after HR round :( , but that day I was confident that yes , I think I have cracked it. It was around 9pm when we left for our home.

Next Day , at 11:11 AM :) We got to know that 8 students have been selected for this role ,And finally the hectic game has finally reached its final Destination .

1. Online Assessment [ 187 candidates appeared for this round ]

Platform: Microsoft Forms (Proctored) Questions: 20 (MCQs) Time: 30 mins Note: There was no auto submit, so make sure to click the submit button before the time ends. Only then your submission will be recorded.

The questions were very basic but it spanned almost all the subjects and topics, from DBMS, CCN, OS, OOPS (guess the output), Programming (Java and C++ and I think 1 question was from C too). Questions were also from Quantitative Aptitude, Logical Reasoning, English (basic grammar, synonyms, antonyms).

Some tips for this round:

1. Keep your basics for these subjects crystal clear. Start preparing for core subjects and aptitude 3-4 months before the season starts. I started late and made some mistakes with earlier companies. So start as early as possible.

2. Revision is the key here. Due to Hyperverge's case study I did not study much for this OA, but my preparation and revision helped. I had made notes in my 2nd year about those subjects. Also I had made formula sheets about Aptitude which helped. So I just revised these things and went for the OA.

3. One important thing I noticed is that the questions were not section-wise so be prepared to see an aptitude question just after an oops question.

My test went pretty well and I was shortlisted for the next round.

2. Digital Interview [ 45 candidates appeared for this round ]

Platform: HireVue Type of Questions: Typical HR and behavioural questions. Time per question: Max 3 mins per question. You can stop the recording once done. Preparation time: 30 seconds before the 3 mins start. Note: There is no button to pause/retry the recording, you have 3 mins to record the answer and a single attempt. You go to the next question after one is done.

Questions that were asked:

1. Why did you choose your current degree program?

2. What do you aim to gain from this internship?

3. Tell us about a challenging project experience.

4. How did you manage multiple priorities and time?

5. Tell us about a time when you realized you have a weakness and how did you try to overcome that?

6. What'd you like us to know more about you?

These questions were the same for everyone.

Some tips for this round:

1. Please focus on speaking and articulating your thoughts well. Try to think how you will structure your answer in the given 30 seconds.

2. Do not make any scripts, or use GPT in any form for making these answers, because that will completely look unnatural.

3. I think they did observe the body language and eye contact with the camera. So try to maintain a good posture, hand movements and good eye contact with the camera. Keep a decent smile (don't overdo) on your face while speaking the answers. Visualize as if you are speaking to a real person, it helps.

3. [Oncampus F2F Interview: Technical Round] [ 34 candidates appeared for this round ]

There were 2 panelists. One of them was fully Technical and the other was both Technical and HR (I think).

We were called at 9:30 am in the morning. The TPCs collected all our resumes before the Interviews began. I was called in, the interview started with an excited greeting and warm welcome from their side. The Panelists were super friendly and since I was a little bit nervous, they fully made me feel comfortable. They first glanced over my resume for 10-20 seconds and then asked me to introduce myself. I had prepared two different kinds of introductions, one for technical and one for HR. I gave the technical one here. I had mentioned Java OOPs in my introduction and resume, so they started with that. They asked to explain in detail, what is OOPs, what the pillars are, and give me examples for each with code. Trick to remember the pillars is: A PIE

Challenge 1: Here I got my first challenge of the Interview. I started with A i.e. Abstraction. I gave an example of a car and its engine and that each engine might have a different implementation, but the programmer need not care about the implementation, he just has to use the defineEngine() method. I then gave the code for it. After this, the Interviewer said take this Car example only and all the remaining pillars! This was the first SHOCK. We usually prepare different examples for each pillar but I think he knew this so he kind of restricted it to a single example to test my understanding. I did not have such examples, but my understanding was very good so I took a couple of mins but made the examples and their code. They were impressed by my understanding and that I on my own insisted on writing the code. Though I do DSA in C++ which is why my Java syntax had a couple of errors. He pointed out that but then I explained to him and he said it is completely fine.

Then they came to my Internship. I had done an internship in GenAI and the project was very unique. They asked me what I did, what was my project (high level explanation followed by technical details), how was the experience, what learnings I got from it etc. They were impressed with the project idea and asked me what is the current status and how are they going to proceed with it (as I had completed my tenure there).

Challenge 2: A DSA question. They then gave me a DSA question. It was: Given a string, delete the minimum number of characters, such that the string becomes a Palindrome. Return this minimum number. You need not return the palindrome string, just the number is enough.

I suggested a two-pointer approach first, where I would just do counter+= 2 when there is a mismatch of characters. I explained it well and wrote the code for it followed by the TC and SC. They were not very satisfied with the approach and gave me an edge case where this solution might fail. It was like: a b a b d a. Here if we compare b and d, then the solution just fails badly. I acknowledged my mistake and asked for a couple of minutes to think of a different solution. After some time, I explained that two pointers might work, we just need to handle such cases. So maybe we can try all ways → that's recursion. I developed an approach quickly with the TC and SC.

I then drew a recursion tree and did a dry run. He seemed satisfied with the response. I was about to write the code but he said, it's okay no problem, we understand the approach, let's move forward.

I was somewhat disappointed in the back of my mind about the question but I tried to focus on what's coming. Next they asked me about my projects. They went really in-depth about every project both from a technical and a business perspective. They also asked about the challenges that I faced in these projects and how I overcame them. So please be ready to answer everything, the how, why, what, when EVERYTHING!

I had links to the Github Repos of all the projects, and they were quite happy to see that. They also asked me whether any of these projects are deployed. One of them was and they opened it. I had deployed my best project and it was also the 1st one in my resume. They opened it, and they were quite satisfied with the UI and initial appearance of the application. Then, bhaai, they tested almost all the features of the application. I prayed to god, please make everything work (haha). They were happy to see that everything was working (though slightly buggy) but they were quite impressed with the project. See make sure if you have deployed something, test everything before your interviews begin. This was a rare case that they checked everything, so be prepared for this too.

At this point, the Interview was going very well and I was very happy.

After this, the female panelist started asking some HR questions like, have you worked in a team? How was the experience? What will you do where there is a conflict in the team? What if you don't like your seniors' approach and you think you have a better way? Some scenarios were also given to me. She was quite impressed with the way I answered the questions with a decent structure and my overall way of speaking and body language.

Some more questions on my projects were asked. The Interview then concluded with the Interviewers asking me if I have any questions for them. I had prepared some questions so I asked them.

1. How is Baker Hughes as an Energy Tech Company using AI? How is AI helping? Any specific projects on which AI is being used?

2. How has Baker Hughes contributed to your personal and professional growth?

We had a healthy discussion on both the questions for some time. Overall the Interview lasted about 50 mins I think.

3. [Oncampus F2F Interview: Techno HR Round] [15 candidates appeared for this round]

As my round 1 ended, within 10-15 mins I was immediately called for round 2. I WAS SO HAPPY !

I entered the room, and to my surprise, there was only 1 panelist and she was the HR I think. Again it started warm greeting and a welcome from her side. She asked me how am I doing, how my day was going and all. The Interview started with the introduction of course. Here I gave the HR introduction. For the HR introduction, make it less technical overall. Like:

1. Your background before SPIT

2. Technical skills but highlight them on a higher level

3. Add your internship learnings than the technical details

4. Finally, blend in your hobbies at the end. Like I did: "when I am not coding or working on my tech projects, you can find me ….."

She complimented me on my introduction! She started asking if I have worked in a team, how was the team, were there any conflicts, how did I resolve them, what was my role in the team etc. Then she gave me a situation: 'Imagine you are working in a team and you are the lead. Now one of your teammates is intentionally not working at the speed which was required, you have to deliver the project to the client tomorrow morning. So you have 1 night, what will you do? How will you handle your team, the client and that one teammate?' Make sure that you have at least some prep to answer such questions. Like I started by highlighting the fact that project is the most important thing here, so I will start by communicating with the team-mate and understand his position and why he is not working. Is there any way I can help him? etc.

Just ensure that you think of some different answers or ways than the most obvious ones. We had a good discussion on this question.

Then since my Internship and projects had a lot of AI, she asked me: 'According to your knowledge about AI from your Internship and projects and your knowledge about Baker Hughes, where do you think Baker Hughes might be using AI?' I asked the exact question in the previous round, so I smartly blended their answer and added some points of my own. She was quite satisfied with my response.

She then asked me why I want to join Baker Hughes, and I prepared an answer for this too so I gave that.

The Interview ended with me asking her the same question I asked in the previous interview.

Overall, I would say my experience in this interview was very positive. I was very happy when I came out and honestly relieved too.

Interview lasted for a good 30 mins I think!

Out of the 15 candidates, 9 were selected and I was one of them!!

journey.howSecured:
Eligibility criteria was 6.5+ CGPA , all branches were allowed.

1. Online Assessment [165 Students appeared for this round ]

● Platform - Microsoft forms (proctored)

● Time - 30mins

● Questions - 25 questions

OA consisted of MCQs based on topics like DBMS, CCN, OS, OOPS, DSA, Cloud Computing, Programming questions (guess the output type) in Python, Java. There were a few Quantitative aptitude questions (work and time, pipe and tank, basic math questions, etc) and Verbal questions (antonyms, synonyms, phrases)

These questions were relatively easy. Time management is key here, dont be stuck on any question for too long. I myself ended up guessing 5-6 questions since there was no negative marking. I suggest preparing for CS fundamentals a month prior to placements and having handy notes to revise whenever required. It may get exhausting studying the same concepts over and over again but trust me it's worth it.

I didn't expect to get selected because I wasn't able to answer a few questions on cloud computing. But luckily got shortlisted for the next round.

2. Digital Interview [45 students were shortlisted for this round]

● Platform - HireVue

● Questions - 6 HR-behavorial questions

● Time - a maximum of 3 mins per question

We received the shortlist around 8pm the same day and were supposed to finish our digital interviews before 3pm the next day. They have been repeating the same set of questions for the last 3 years now, so there's high chances they will repeat the same.

Questions were as follows:

1. Why did you choose your current degree program?

2. What do you aim to gain from this internship?

3. Tell us about a challenging project experience.

4. How did you manage multiple priorities and time?

5. Tell us about a time when you realized you have a weakness and how did you try to overcome that?

6. What'd you like us to know more about you?

I had prepared a couple of points that I would like to mention for each of these questions, but not an entire script. I suggest being as natural as possible throughout the interview and staying confident. It is okay if you fumble a little -- just be confident enough to recover from it and don't let it affect your overall presence.

A few important tips:

1. Wear formal attire.

2. Sit in a quiet, secluded room with no disturbances.

3. Use headphones to ensure good sound quality.

3. Technical Interview [ 35 students appeared for this round]

My interview lasted for approximately 40 minutes. I had two interviewers on my panel: a Product Manager and a Data Scientist at Baker Hughes. The interview began with greetings and some small talk about the heavy rains that day. After that, they asked me to introduce myself. This wasn't something I had scripted; I just had an outline in mind of what I wanted to cover. My suggestion here would be to mention things you are very confident about, as the first few questions are usually follow-ups to your introduction. You are the one who decides the flow of the interview so answer thoughtfully and only discuss topics you know inside out.

In my case, I mentioned my Smart India Hackathon win, a few other hackathons, and the conference paper I had published. They then asked me several technical questions about my SIH project, including explaining the entire system architecture and data flow.

A couple of my projects involved LLMs, so they asked me to explain how transformers work. Since I had studied this thoroughly, I spent a good amount of time explaining it in detail I explained the architecture starting with the encoder-decoder structure, the role of embeddings. I went over the concept of self-attention--how queries, keys, and values interact to determine contextual importance for each token--and explained multi-head attention, layer normalization, and feedforward layers, using ChatGPT as an example to make it more relatable. One of the interviewers was well-acquainted with transformer models and its working, so he actively asked me "why" and "how" questions about each layer, which made the discussion engaging.

After that, they moved on to basic Python questions, such as the difference between arrays, sets, and lists, and asked me to give examples of when I would use each. They then shifted to OOPS concepts--asking me the difference between object-oriented programming and procedural programming. I couldn't give a very detailed explanation but provided a brief overview, which seemed to satisfy them. They also asked me to explain what OOPS is and why it is needed, which was a straightforward question.

The last 5 mins of my interview were around discussing my internships, my contribution in each and also my leadership experience as the Vice Chair of IEEE-SPIT - This part felt more like a friendly conversation than a formal interview.

4. HR Interview [ 15 students appeared for this round]

I was called for the HR interview immediately after my first interview. It was quite short, lasting no more than 15 minutes. The HR interviewer asked me to introduce myself and then asked a few questions about my projects. After that, she moved on to situational questions:

1. What would you do if a client disapproved of a project you had been working on for months and asked you to redo it?

2. What would you do if you were at a hackathon and your project didn't work during the final demo?

My biggest advice here is to carefully understand the question and, if possible, relate it to a past experience. For example, I had gone through a situation similar to the second question, so it was easy for me to relate to it and explain my thought process.

Overall, my HR interview went really well--it didn't feel like an interview at all, but more like a conversation. The key is to stay calm and confident, and most importantly, be yourself. They are not looking for textbook answers; they want authentic, personal responses. So be honest and answer with confidence.

9 students received the offer.

1. Know your Resume INSIDE OUT:- Make sure you have at least some ideas about each and every word written on your resume. Please do not write anything that you have no idea about, it will create a very bad impression

2. DSA and Fundamental concepts are Important:- It is always good to be prepared about anything and everything. My personal recommendation is that when there is time do problems from both Leetcode as well as from CodeForces as it will help you in coming up and implement ing of solutions. Also keep your knowled ge of fundamental subjects clear.

3. Practice Aptitude:- Use IndiaBix for aptitude.

4. Build Projects that have some value:- Do not build generic projects, try to see what real-world problems can you solve and try to solve that in your projects. It may not be perfect, but is still way better than something too generic. Also try to keep a solid reason ready on why you chose a particular xyz technology over something else.

5. Have a general idea of all projects and your role etc. But practice one project in deep and use it everywhere for questioning and cross questioning.

6. Consistency and Discipline are of paramount importance:- Whatever you do, stay consistent with it. I remember, when starting out, I used to get anxious when I couldn't solve a problem, but with time and effort, I did manage to solve those.

7. Communication is unparallelly important!

8. There will be times when things will just not work out.

9. Use an ATS Friendly Overleaf Resume Template.

10. Lastly, do not lose hope if you are not selected, keep on trying.

Get used to rejections. Do not give up. During the entire placement season keep your health up and your overall attitude positive, had severe side effects that caused excruciating joint pains, and still had to travel 1 hour daily for online assessments and interviews. I faced rejections in interviews from Nomura, and in the HR round of ISS, during Wissen's 2nd round.

Stay connected to your friends. They can help more than you can imagine, they conduct mock interviews, help build projects together, prepare in groups. It really helps in keeping the momentum and staying motivated.

HR Interview Tips:

1. Maintain Eye Contact Ensure steady, natural eye contact with the interviewer. It shows confidence and helps build a connection, but avoid staring as it may come across as forced.

2. Be Mindful of What You Share Avoid oversharing personal experiences that do not directly address the question. Focus on relevant, concise answers that highlight your suitability for the role.

3. Use the STAR Method Structure your answers to behavioral questions using the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result). It provides clarity and demonstrates a problem-solving mindset.

4. Show Respect in All Responses Be polite and professional. Even casual or off-topic comments should be delivered respectfully to avoid unintentionally offending the interviewer.

5. Frame Strengths and Weaknesses as Narratives Share your strengths and weaknesses with context. Use short stories or examples (real or carefully crafted) that showcase growth and self-awareness.

6. Avoid Monologues Do not treat your answers like speeches. Keep the conversation balanced, concise, and interactive. Know when to stop and where to elaborate.

7. Display Confidence and Personality Strong communication and soft skills often outweigh technical skills in HR rounds. Let your personality come through--be confident, composed, and clear.

8. Always be Positive Always answer all questions in a positive manner and I will suggest do not ask for feedback in an HR interview, you can in a technical round if you feel that you have done great.

9. Always Deny plans for Higher Studies Never show interest or accidently hint your passion for academia and research. Prepare solid reasons to justify why you are choosing industry over academia, or it may become your reason for rejection.

Just work hard and you will succeed eventually, it is never over until you give up. Rome wasn't built in a day, it was built gradually so will your career for the day you give up on yourself is the day you lose.

Keep your outlook positive and have faith there is some opportunity kept explicitly for you and when it comes it will come served on a silver platter for you.

ALL THE BEST!!!

Feel free to contact me on LinkedIn

In case of any further doubts, you can refer to the past interview experiences shared by TPO.

If at any point you lose your momentum things can go into a spiral. Keep yourself motivated the placement process can be hectic a times even frustrating but it's up to you to keep yourself going.

2. Digital Interview [45 students appeared] (on the 12th August till 3:30pm):-

Platform:- HireVue Type of Questions:- Typical HR and behavioral questions. Time per question:- Max 3 mins per question. You can stop the recording once done. Preparation time:- 30 seconds before the 3 mins start.

Note:- There is no button to pause/retry the recording, you have 3 mins to record the answer and a single attempt. You go to the next question after you answer and voluntarily procced or timer times out . There were a few trials available before starting to answer any of the actual question.

Questions that were asked:

1. Why did you choose your current degree program?

2. What do you aim to gain from this internship?

3. Tell us about a challenging project experience.

4. How did you manage multiple priorities and time?

5. Tell us about a time when you realized you have a weakness and how did you try to overcome that?

6. What would you like us to know more about you? These questions were the same for everyone.

Some tips for this round:

1. Please focus on speaking and articulating your thoughts well. Structure your well answer in the given 30 seconds.

2. Do not read any scripts, or use GPT in any form for making these answers, because that will definitely look unnatural if you read onto the camera, it can easily be captured.

3. They do observe the body language and eye contact with the camera so try to maintain a good posture, hand movements and good eye contact with the camera. Keep a decent smile (do not overdo) on your face while speaking the answers.

4. Visualize as if you are speaking to a real person, if it helps.

5. Most importantly be confident about what you are speaking, be clear on what you wish to convey, be natural and have a positive outlook do not prolong any answer unnecessarily.

3. Technical Interview [35 students appeared] (on the 14th of August in college):-

We were called at 9:30 am in the morning. The TPCs collected all our resumes before the Interviews began and handed each interview panelist a copy before beginning. I was the 1st person for my panel; the interview began with me exchanging warm greetings with the 2 panelists. They asked me to introduce myself while they glanced at my resume. They picked up my interest for cyber security from my introduction and in continuation to it asked about my cyber security project on my resume. They asked me to explain them like they had little to no knowledge of cyber security. I explained them keeping their request in mind (I was used to interviewers with no idea asking

me to explain it) but then the tables turned one of them started going into depth of it and asked about why I choose it and not something different (at this point it dawned on me that this panel is well versed in cyber security) we discuss ed on these lines for about ~40 minutes. After this they asked me a few HR questions like did I attend the ppt to which I told them the truth that I wasn 't as I was late and the room was full, they asked me the 4 pillars of Baker Hughes to which I answered 2 and tried to think but later confessed on not remembering them. They seemed satisfied and said I could leave. At this juncture I asked the panelist if he was working in cyber security as no interviewer up to now had an idea of what I was speaking to which the grim on his face broadened and answered affirmatively then I proceeded to ask him how seriously does Baker Hughes take cyber security after which I asked their permission to leave.

4. Techo-HR Interview [15 students appeared] (on the 14th of August in college):-

After around 20 mins of finishing my 1 st round, I was called for my 2nd round. The TPC's did the same drill collecting a resume copy and handing it to the 2nd panel, this panel too had 2 panelists. The questions in this round were more HR with typical questions like:-

1. How was your day?

2. If I walk into a class ad ask your friends, what will they say about you?

3. What is the thing(s) that all your friends do dislike about you?

4. Then how did you handle conflict in a group?

5. One thing that you had to do because none of your teammates were willing to do?

And so on. Overall it was a 40-45 min endeavor.

Finally, 9 Students were offered the job me being one of them.

1. Know your Resume INSIDE OUT:- Make sure you have at least some ideas about each and every word written on your resume. Please do not write anything that you have no idea about, it will create a very bad impression

5. Have a general idea of all projects and your role etc. But practice one project in deep and use it everywhere for questioning and cross questioning.

6. Consistency and Discipline are of paramount importance:- Whatever you do, stay consistent with it. I remember, when starting out, I used to get anxious when I couldn't solve a problem, but with time and effort, I did manage to solve those.

7. Communication is unparallelly important!

8. There will be times when things will just not work out.

9. Use an ATS Friendly Overleaf Resume Template.

Eligibility Criteria was 6.5+ CGPA, No Backlogs and Resume shortlisting. All branches were eligible (not sure about MCA).

1. OA Round [167 candidates appeared, 46 shortlisted] (Invigilation was done by the company)

Platform: Microsoft forms

Duration: 30 mins

No. of questions: 25

The test consisted of topics covering SQL, output based questions (python/Java), Aptitude, OS, CCN, DSA, Cloud Computing. If you have a strong grip on CS core subjects, this test would be comparatively easier for you. Time management is key so attempt confident questions first, then move to elimination or educated guesses. I hadn't prepared for Cloud Computing and CCN well, which had cost me several marks, so make sure to cover these areas as well. (My story: After discussing with friends after the test, I was convinced I wouldn't be shortlisted. My dukh-daard-peedha continued, and with a heavy heart I went off to Taco Bell for lunch. To my surprise, while eating, I got an email from Baker Hughes saying I was shortlisted for the digital interview round. That instantly lifted my mood and I left for home and started preparing for it. So guys, don't lose hope until results are declared ;) )

2. Digital Interview [46 candidates appeared, 35 shortlisted]

This was conducted on the Hire Vue platform same as JMPC CFG. Below were the questions asked, these people are asking the same questions from the past two years so chances are they might repeat. Those who aren't familiar with this platform, it is basically an AI who would be taking your interview. The question will be displayed on the screen and you will be given 30 secs to prepare for it, then you need to record your answer for 3 mins but you can stop anytime you complete giving your answer. They are basic HR questions. The company's people will be evaluating later as well. The questions were:

1. Why did you choose your current degree program?

2. What do you aim to gain from this internship?

3. Tell us about a challenging project experience.

4. How did you manage multiple priorities and time?

5. Tell us about a time when you realized you have a weakness and how did you try to overcome that?

6. What'd you like us to know more about you?

Tip: Try to include as many keywords of the company's values as possible. And give answers from personal experiences. Don't try to read it from script, speak naturally.

( My Story: We had a deadline at 3 PM, so I sat for my interview around 2 PM. Just as I began answering the first question, the doorbell rang. Since I stay in a PG, I assumed someone else would open it. But it rang again, and that broke my flow and I ended up fumbling through the next two questions. Lesson: if you live in a PG, inform your roommates beforehand and handle distractions like the doorbell early on. Also, choose the quietest spot possible and keep your phone on silent. After this shaky start, I honestly had no hopes of being shortlisted for further rounds. They sent the shortlist by 13th of August, and as expected my name was not included in the list. Devastated, demotivated and feeling lost, I started evaluating my next company's options. In the next hour, they sent an additional shortlist with 3 students' names included and my prayers were answered, my name was in that. It turned out 3 people in the original list were already placed so they removed them and included the next 3 :D. I spent the entire night going through my resume and revising CS fundamentals. )

3. Technical Round [ 35 students appeared, 16 shortlisted ]

The offline interview was scheduled on 14th August, divided into 6 panels around 9:30 in the morning. And I was the first one to get interviewed in my panel. My panel consisted of two people, one sir was from AIML domain and there was another ma'am who was specializing in DevOps. It started on a light note with them asking, how I was feeling and how was the process till now for me. Then they asked for my introduction. Remember guys your introduction decides the flow for the rest of the interview, it should include your name, branch, proficiency in which languages, and your interest. I also included my projects and extracurricular activities, as well as my hackathon wins. Since Baker Hughes focused on sustainability and leadership, I had two projects related to it and my committee work to showcase those values. Then he asked to explain my first project, EcoVerse and focused on one particular feature which included giving ecofriendly alternatives of everyday products. I explained how we had scraped the data from another website and were using keyword based retrieval to display in the frontend. Then he asked me what if product category was not included in the dataset, then how would you classify the items, considering the same product can have different names with different brands, and also told me it was a large dataset which would simultaneously add new products on the fly. First, I came about the semantic similarity approach, which would retrieve on the basis of semantic meaning behind the product name so that even if the product has different names if their meaning is same they would still be considered equal, but they didn't seem satisfied with it. So, I thought about it for a minute and told them I would use KNN algorithm which would group similar products in one cluster and if a new datapoint were to arrive it would give recommendations with the nearest clusters. He later assured me that I was going in the right direction and asked me to come up with an approach that doesn't include a labelled dataset, so I said I would use K-means in that case and then asked me to explain the entire algorithm. The interviewers seemed satisfied with it. Later, he noticed I had a project that included OCR, so he inquired about what it does, and what challenges I will face if I worked on a real world dataset. I gave some problems, but he expected more, so I genuinely confessed as we had worked on a very structured dataset, these are the only problems we faced in our project. This seemed to convince him a bit. Later, he jumped

on some HR questions and asked what would I do if I were to get assigned to a monotonous task in the project? Then seeing how I had included React in almost all of my projects, inquired about why React and not Angular? I explained how I wanted to learn how to build end to end projects so after learning React, I shifted my focus on getting hands on backend development. Then ma'am asked me about my role as Carnival Executive head, why did I approach influencers as judges because in this generation anyone can be an influencer. To this I answered we onboarded only those influencers who have won some beauty pageant to have some relevance. She also asked if I had ever come across a situation where there was dispute in a group project and how did I handle it, what was my mindset? Then sir asked why I used MongoDB in my project and what was the need for it and its schema. Later the interview shifted to SQL, as I had mentioned in my introduction that I am proficient in it. He started off with basic questions, the difference between drop and truncate. Then asked which is faster delete or truncate. I answered truncate would be faster because delete includes a where condition, then he questioned me what if delete didn't have any condition then which would be faster, to this I again answered truncate but he looked at me doubtfully, so I confessed I was not sure. (Although later I found out I was right, he wanted an explanation but I was just giving an educated guess :P). Then I was asked how I would retrieve a unique row to which I first answered using the primary key of the table and select query, she later changed the question to unique values to which I answered using distinct keyword. Then I was asked the difference between rank and dense rank. It ended with them asking if I had any questions for them. I inquired how many years they have been working for Baker Hughes and what motivated them to join the company. (Bit of a bold move on my part xD, but they seemed to laugh it off and answered me.) This round lasted for about an hour for me.

I was not asked any questions related to DSA, OS, CCN some of the other students were asked in other panels. Including unique projects on your resume helps divert their attention there more, so try building such projects. And know the in and out about everything mentioned in your resume, even though it's a group project, it's important to know the entire flow of the project.

4. Leadership Round [16 candidates appeared, 9 were selected]

Within an hour of finishing my first round, I was called in for the second. Many candidates were still waiting to give their first, but that's the advantage of being among the earliest in your panel, make a good impression and you are set for the next round. The interview started off with her asking how my initial rounds of interviews went. I frankly answered that I wasn't expecting it to turn out this way and me coming to the final round. She was curious as to why I had this mindset. To which I told her about my previous experiences and how I used to get really nervous answering questions and was not able to clear other companies first rounds. So she asked what changed now. I answered I decided to just trust myself and god and go with the flow. I was asked to explain my favourite project, then asked me how many people were a part of it, I answered two. She asked what I would do if my teammate was not cooperating. Also asked situational questions if I were the product manager and the tech team has informed me that they won't be able to deliver the product in the given deadline, how would I handle this situation? Remember transparency and reliable product delivery are the core company values so answer these questions in that regard. Also, asked follow up questions like if the client was not ready to extend the deadline what would you do? To this I answered, I would first negotiate with the client if it were possible to drop certain functionalities so the tech team can speed up the process, because giving a non functioning and untested product is not a viable option. Then she noticed that I had used Power BI in one of my data analysis projects and asked me to explain it and later inquired if I knew any other power apps to which I honestly replied no. Later, questions about which upi app I used and why, if I could add

one more feature on it, what would it be were asked. She also put forth a technical question related to frauds happening on such apps and how would I handle them. The interview ended on a high note with me getting a chance to ask about her experience working for Baker Hughes, and she seemed very interested in answering my questions.

I was done with my interview and was waiting for the results. The process ended around 6 pm in the evening with 9 candidates receiving the offer. I was just glad to be one of them 😀

Total 3 rounds: Online Assessment, Technical Interview, and HR Interview.

1. Online Assessment [90-100 students appeared]

The round consisted of four secƟons: Logical ApƟtude, QuanƟtaƟve ApƟtude, Coding, and a Verbal SecƟon. Everyone received two diﬀerent coding quesƟons, and the diﬃculty level was quite random. Some students received easy quesƟons involving HashSets or HashMaps, while others got diﬃcult Dynamic Programming (DP) quesƟons.

Thankfully, I received very easy quesƟons:

1. Remove duplicate elements from an array and return the unique elements.

2. Count the frequency of each character in a string.

Tips:

 PracƟcing apƟtude quesƟons from IndiaBix and GeeksforGeeks (GFG) is suﬃcient. Just remember the paƩerns and formulas to solve similar types of problems.

 These paƩerns are repeƟƟve in every Online Assessment, just presented in diﬀerent forms.

 For Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA), start pracƟcing as soon as possible. I regret starƟng only one month before placements.

 However, if you are starƟng late as I did, you can sƟll succeed. BeƩer late than never, but I sƟll recommend starƟng your DSA preparaƟon a minimum of six months in advance.

 There are students who get beƩer oﬀers without pracƟcing more than 10 DSA quesƟons, but this is an excepƟon and relies on luck, so don't depend on it.

2. Technical Interview [32 candidates appeared for this round]

My technical interview was unique. It's important to know that everything depends on the panel you are assigned to. There were three panels, with two panelists in each. The diﬃculty level and types of quesƟons were not standardized across all students. You will realize this aŌer a few interviews. My panel was very relaxed.

They didn't ask me for a formal introducƟon. Instead, they asked how my preparaƟon was going, how I had prepared for TransUnion, when I started, and if I had spoken with any seniors from my college who work at the company. You might think these are easy quesƟons, but your answers, where you might menƟon various technologies to impress them, will determine the direcƟon of the interview. I didn't menƟon DSA or SQL in my answers because I was not conﬁdent in my skills in those areas.

The interviewer then asked me to explain my projects. This is a quesƟon asked in every interview, so you should have 100% knowledge of your projects. Mostly, the interview will focus on the ﬁrst project listed on your resume, and someƟmes a second one. AŌer I explained my project, they presented some edge cases and asked how I would handle large amounts of data and improve the execuƟon Ɵme.

Then, they asked me how I would handle a Git conﬂict and what prompt I would give to ChatGPT to help resolve it. Next, they asked how I would run the project on another system. I answered with "Docker," which led them to ask more in-depth quesƟons about cloud compuƟng. However, I stopped them and explained that I haven't worked with cloud compuƟng technologies and don't have much knowledge about it. It's okay to admit when you don't know the answer to a quesƟon. Don't try to give a wrong answer; just be honest. However, you shouldn't say "I don't know" for every quesƟon.

They also asked about a hackathon I parƟcipated in: why my team placed in the top 10 and not ﬁrst, what went wrong, and what I learned from the experience. Then, they asked me to explain Docker to a layman with no technical knowledge. The interviewer was quite impressed with my analogy. Finally, he asked if I had any quesƟons for them. I asked them 3-4 quesƟons. The interview lasted for 27 minutes.

Tips:

 When you enter the room, greet them with a smile and a handshake.

 Give your introducƟon conﬁdently because the ﬁrst impression is the last impression.

 You should know the in-depth meaning of every word on your resume. It's not about the number of technologies you list, but how well you know them.

 There are standard quesƟons asked about projects, such as: how you would handle a large amount of data, how you would scale the system, why you used a speciﬁc technology, and how you would improve performance.

 You are the driver of the interview, so the conversaƟon will likely follow the direcƟon you set with your answers.

 I wasn't conﬁdent in DSA and puzzles, so I avoided menƟoning them. However, this completely depends on the panel. Other companies or panels will deﬁnitely ask more technical quesƟons on CS fundamentals like OS, OOPS, DSA, and DBMS.

 If there are two interviewers, try to maintain eye contact with both. Keep a smile on your face to show conﬁdence.

 They oŌen prioriƟze moƟvaƟon and a posiƟve mindset over just technical experƟse.

 Ask for their names at the end if they didn't introduce themselves at the beginning.

p

3. HR Interview [10-12 candidates selected for this round]

There was one panel with two panelists. Both were very relaxed. They started with small talk, asking how my day was going and if I'd had lunch. Then, they asked me to introduce myself, focusing on aspects not menƟoned in my resume.

When asked to explain my project, I didn't get too technical. Instead, I focused on storytelling: how I got the idea, my approach, how I collaborated with my team, and the project's future scope.

They then asked about my family background, if I had any issues with relocaƟon, why they should hire me, and if I had plans for a master's degree. Finally, they asked if I had any quesƟons for them. I asked a couple of quesƟons and made sure to shake their hands before leaving, as I had forgoƩen to do so at the start.

[8 students received an oﬀer including me]

Tips:

 I saw many people with good technical knowledge who were not selected aŌer the HR interview.

 Therefore, try to improve your English ﬂuency. I understand if you don't come from an English-medium background (Like me), but at least try to speak conﬁdently, even if you make a few grammaƟcal mistakes.

 Always smile during the interview.

 I feel that the HR interview is about engaging the interviewers with your communicaƟon skills, like telling a story about your projects and your learnings. Don't dive deep into technical terms; they are generally not concerned with those details.

 Try to show them what a good team player you are.

 Conﬁdence, a smile, and honesty are the keys to succeeding in the HR interview.

I gave the brute-force solution, and was prepared to give the optimal answer if they asked but they didn't ask me to optimize further.

One interviewer then asked about AI, ML, and DL, and how I would approach building a chatbot for student queries. But only if it's not on your resume.

Then I was asked to rate myself in SQL, explain normalization, and give an example. I created a table and applied 1NF, and they said that was enough. I was asked about joins and they also asked me to write a query to find the top 10 students with the highest marks.

They gave me the Lion, Goat, and Grass puzzle, which I already knew, but I clarified the rules before explaining the solution.

Towards the end, I was asked about a challenge I faced in my project, so I shared how I resolved a feature issue in my major project. Finally, I asked the interviewers about their roles and whether there was anything I should start learning that would help me if I joined TransUnion. They suggested a few technologies they use at TransUnion.

Since the PPT had mentioned a budget for learning and certifications, I asked about that and that concluded the round.

8 students got the offer in the end.

Placement Process:

The recruitment process had 3 stages; Online Assessment, Technical Interview and HR Interview. The Pre-Placement talk was carried out at SPIT, in-person by the TransUnion team, prior to the Online Assessment.

1. [Online Assessment] [ 87 students appeared for this round ]
journey.prep:
Here are some resources I used for interview preparation:

Using all of these for preparation as early as possible is important. Start at most 6 months before the placement period begins. Ensure you know every single programming language and framework on your resume as much as possible. Also, add good projects to your resumes. Ones that solve real-world problems, and are innovative and unique. Ensure they are uploaded to your Github account or, even better, deployed on a public URL. Doing an internship before the placement period is also recommended.

For DSA: Use Striver's A2Z DSA course https://takeuforward.org/strivers-a2z-dsa-course/strivers-a2z-dsa-course-sheet-2/

For OOPS, DBMS, OS: Use https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/

For Git/Github and Computer Networks: Watch Kunal Kushwaha's videos. https://www.youtube.com/@KunalKushwaha

For Aptitude: Solve questions from https://www.indiabix.com/

For SQL questions: Use SQL 50 from Leetcode and keep solving from the SQL section. SQLBolt is a good resource for beginners.

For System Design: Watch Gaurav Sen's videos: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SqcXvc3ZmRU&list=PLMCXHnjXnTnvo6alSjVkgxV-VH6EPyvoX&a b_channel=GauravSen

⚠ A Final Note:

Placements are heavily dependent on luck, 80-90% of the process is. Luck decides which questions you get in the test, what sort of interviewer you get, what mood they are in, etc. Many people better than me were unplaced at the time of me typing this sheet out. The only thing you can do is work as hard as you can to maximize your luck at any point. I had applied for 16 companies on campus, getting rejected in 4 interviews, and unable to clear 12 OAs. All it needs is one breakthrough.

If not now, then some company will take you up later. If you see your friends get placed before yourself, it's completely natural to feel dejected. The important thing is to remember that you aren't any worse than those around you for not getting selected yet. Just remain calm, do not underestimate yourself, do not keep any excessive expectations (since they can cause pressure) and keep yourself disciplined throughout this hectic period. Take frequent breaks, meditate, and get outdoor time. It is important.

Some online tests are not proctored. No matter how tempting it may seem, DO NOT CHEAT, you will end up paying for it sooner or later (not my own experience FYI). Work hard and get placed on the basis of your merits.

Alright, that's my experience! I hope it gave some valuable insights and was of help to you. Feel free to contact me on my LinkedIn.

☆ Remember to trust the process! ☆

The recruitment process had 3 stages; Online Assessment, Technical Interview and HR Interview. The Pre-Placement talk was carried out at SPIT, in-person by the TransUnion team, prior to the Online Assessment.

1. [Online Assessment] [ 87 students appeared for this round ]

On the basis of their resumes, 87 candidates were shortlisted for the test out of those who applied for TransUnion. The test was conducted on 4th September. It lasted for 1 h 30 min, from 14 00 to 15 30. The test was conducted on SHL and calculators were allowed. There were 4 sections in the test:

Mathematical Aptitude. Puzzle and Pattern based Aptitude. Coding section. English Vocabulary and Grammar section.

A. Mathematical Aptitude involved questions like ratios, proportion, simple interest, time, etc. Example:

● If a train travels 120 km in 2 hours, how long will it take to travel 300 km at the same speed?

● Divide ₹720 among A, B, and C in the ratio 2:3:4.

B. Puzzle and Pattern-based Aptitude involved questions like finding the odd one out, guessing the next number, etc. Example:

● Find the odd one out: 121, 144, 169, 196, 225, 242

● What comes next in the series: 2, 4, 8, 16, ?

C. The English vocabulary consisted of questions like finding the correct sentence or understanding the conveyed message from a passage. Example:

● Choose the grammatically correct sentence: A) He don't like playing cricket.

B) He doesn't likes playing cricket. C) He doesn't like playing cricket.

● From the given passage, what is the main idea the author is trying to convey?

D. Coding questions consisted of 2 questions of varying difficulty. I received 2 fairly easy questions.

Q1: You are given an array of orders. Find the Order ID of every order in the array. (There was a lot more to the question, I forgot the rest, sorry about that guys :P) Solution: The order ID is calculated by summing all the digits of each element in the array. (The question was framed in a confusing manner, making it seem more difficult than it actually was. I got the solution by analysing the results which followed that format.) Example: Input: [123, 56, 89] Output: [6 (1+2+3), 11 (5+6), 17 (8+9)]

Q2: You are given a 1-indexed array of people with labels 1 to n. For the next m turns, you have to swap the people with specified labels (e.g., '1, 5' means swap 1 and 5's place). After m swaps, return the person at kth index. Example:

● Initial array: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

● Swaps: [(1, 5), (2, 4)] After swaps: [5, 4, 3, 2, 1]

● If k = 1, return 5.

Tip: For the Online Assessments, I would suggest doing timed practice of aptitude questions and coding questions too. Be sure to practice CodeForces questions as their style (the way they accept inputs and return outputs) can be quite different from LeetCode questions.

2. [Technical Interview] [ 32 students appeared for this round ]

The interviews began the very next day, on 5th September, 10 00 onwards. There were 3 panels, with each containing 2 people who would interview you at the same time. I entered and greeted the panelists. The 2 panelists asked me to introduce myself. I stated my name, where I was studying, and I gave them a brief, yet comprehensive overview of my projects. They asked which programming language I am most comfortable with, which framework I use the most, which frameworks I have used that contain my main programming language, and 'who was the last person you argued with?'

About my projects, they asked me what ML model I used in one, what is the full-form of OCR (since one of my projects had it) and some other surface-level questions.

Then came a DSA question. It was 'You have an array containing elements. Find all of the duplicate elements. Eg: Input: [1,2,3,6,1,1,4,2,2,2,9], Output: [1,2]'. I stated that we can use a hashmap, traverse the entire array, and implement a frequency counter for each element. After that, we use another for loop on the hashmap to select any element which has a frequency over 1. They asked me the time complexity and whether it could be optimised.

They asked me about Object-Oriented Programming. I stated that I was more comfortable with OOP in Java than in Python. Then they asked me to state what pointers are and the difference between Byte and byte in Java.

Finally, an SQL question. We have a table, and we want to delete records containing email of a certain value. We had to write the SQL query on paper. I was also asked how SQL tables reduce query runtimes in case of extremely large tables, to which I replied 'indexing'. They also asked for the explanation of indexing, which I gave along with a real-life analogy.

Lastly, they asked me whether I had any questions for them. I asked them what goes on behind-the-scenes before TransUnion decides to venture or expand into a new area or sector, how they decide whether it is worth venturing into or not. They liked the question and gave a rough idea since they didn't have the answer to this, being software developers, they weren't in charge of these decisions.

Finally, I shook hands firmly with them as I got up, thanking them for their time and closing the door behind me as I left.

The interview lasted only 15-20 minutes. (Every other applicant was surprised, too, since interviews last for 30-45 minutes on average.)

Tips:

Be confident and explain everything clearly. To explain your projects in detail without going on for too long, preferably use an established method like the STAR method.

If you don't know something, DO NOT go on a long-winded, vague explanation in hopes that it will be correct. Just say you don't know it, or you have done it, but forgotten, and the interviewers will move on to the next question. (I did so with the Byte vs byte question and the optimization technique for the DSA question).

The above point also applies to answers you are unsure about. Be confident and stick with some answer. Interviewers test your conviction and willpower, they don't expect you to know everything they ask anyway.

Know your resume in and out. Explain your projects properly and clearly, without sounding too vague. Do not fake anything in it.

When explaining your DSA question's solution, state and explain your thought process as if it were a tutorial of some sort, rather than going silent completely. Start with the brute force-approach and then provide an optimised solution if prompted.

3. [HR Round] [ Approximately 12 students appeared for this round ]

I was asked basic HR questions. I introduced myself, and explained my projects along too, hence they asked questions about the projects on my resume. These questions weren't about the tech and more about what I considered before implementing features in them. They asked me about general limitations that could arise in my project and how I would deal with them.

They moved on to ask me about my family, about their occupations, where I stay, which location I would like, and whether I was open to relocation. Then, they proceeded to ask me why I wanted to work at TransUnion, what my greatest strength is, and how I became good at it. I was also asked why I chose AIML in engineering.

The interview ended with me asking the interviewers the same question I asked in the first interview round (since I got only a rough answer). They answered it in greater detail and I shook hands firmly with them as I got up, thanking them for their time and closing the door behind me as I left.

The interview lasted 15-20 minutes.

Important Tip: Be attentive during the pre-placement talk. Take notes if need be. You MUST remain familiar with what the company does, their values, and what they expect from the average applicant, be it technical skills or soft skills. Work on your communication skills. Even if you have good knowledge, how you convey it might make the difference. Take part in mock interviews and mock speeches to reduce nervousness.

4. [Final Round] [ 8 students appeared for this round ]

Everyone was called outside the TPO and made to sit in room 105, including the TPCs. The TransUnion team entered and stated that only 2 students were selected. The remaining 6 had to go home.

Just kidding. This was a prank round.

All 8 people who cleared the HR round were selected for TransUnion.

[ 8 students were offered the job ]

The selection process consisted of the following rounds:

1. Pre-Placement Talk (PPT) The PPT was conducted offline and began a little late as all the company team members had not yet arrived. During this time, the HR ma'am interacted with us informally and invited five volunteers to perform a short skit. I was one of the participants in this activity. I advise actively participating in such activities, as they showcase confidence, help during the HR rounds, and leave a positive impression on the recruiters.

Afterward, the company representatives delivered their presentation, providing a detailed introduction about the organization, its work culture, and the career opportunities available. I would also suggest asking relevant doubts and clarifying queries during the PPT, as it demonstrates genuine interest in the company and further strengthens your impression.

2. Online Assessment [87 students appeared for this round]

The Test was conducted on 4th September from 14:00 to 15:30 (1 hour 30 minutes). The test was hosted on SHL, and calculators were allowed. It consisted of four sections:

1. Logical Aptitude: Easy to medium-level questions, including puzzles and pattern-based problems such as finding the odd one out or guessing the next number. Example questions included: o Find the odd one out: 121, 144, 169, 196, 225, 242 o What comes next in the series: 2, 4, 8, 16, ? 14 questions were to be solved in 14 minutes.

2. Quantitative Aptitude: Questions on topics like ratios, proportions, simple interest, and time & work. Example questions: o If a train travels 120 km in 2 hours, how long will it take to travel 300 km at the same speed? o Divide ₹720 among A, B, and C in the ratio 2:3:4 12 questions were to be solved in 12 minutes.

3. Coding Section: Two coding questions were provided, with difficulty varying randomly among candidates. o My questions were:

1. Count the frequency of special characters in a string.

2. Count the frequency of numbers in a given number. 50 minutes were allotted for this section.

4. Verbal/English Section: Questions focused on grammar, vocabulary, and comprehension. Example: o Choose the grammatically correct sentence: ▪ He don't like playing cricket. ▪ He doesn't likes playing cricket. ▪ He doesn't like playing cricket. o Understand the main idea conveyed in a passage. 12 questions were to be solved in 14 minutes.

Note: The coding section difficulty varied significantly for different students. Some received easy questions involving HashSets or HashMaps, while others got challenging Dynamic Programming problems. My experience was comparatively easier, as my questions focused on counting frequencies, which I could solve efficiently within the time limit.

Tip: Start practicing aptitude questions well before placements, as most companies include them in their selection process. Additionally, regularly practice Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) to handle coding sections efficiently.

3. Technical Round [32 students appeared for this round] [30-35 mins]

I. Introduction and Projects

• The interview began with a general introduction, followed by a discussion of my projects.

• Projects and Challenges: I was asked to explain all my projects in detail and describe the challenges I faced during implementation.

• Language Preference: The interviewer inquired about my preferred programming languages and which ones I was most proficient in.

II. Java and C++ Deep Dive The main technical discussion focused on my Java project.

• Core Java Questions: o Why I chose Java for the project. o Key differences between Java and C++. o How Java achieves platform independence. o Which file is generated upon Java code execution. o The role of JVM and JRE in making Java platform-independent.

• Memory Management in Java (Interview Q&A): The interviewer asked about types of memory in Java. I explained that the primary memory areas relevant for program execution are Heap and Stack: o Heap: Stores all objects and class instances created at runtime. o Stack: Stores local variables, method call frames, and references to objects in the heap.

o Example: In public static void main(String[] args), local variables like integers or references are stored on the stack, while objects created using new inside main are stored on the heap.

III. Data Structures (Scenario-Based) The interviewer presented real-life scenarios and asked which data structure I would use.

Scenario 1: Stock Market Prices

• Scenario: You are developing an application to track stock market prices throughout the day. You need to quickly retrieve the price of a stock at specific integer times, such as 9, 10, 11… 3.

• Question: Which data structure would you use to efficiently store and retrieve these prices, and why?

Scenario 2: Digital Signature (Undo/Redo)

• Scenario: You have developed an application where, at the final step, the user needs to provide a digital signature. If the user creates a signature but is not satisfied, they can clear it and create a new one. Later, they realize that the previous signature was better.

• Question: How would you retrieve the previous signature? Which data structure would you use and why?

IV. Coding and Problem Solving (Palindrome)

• Problem: Check if a given string is a palindrome. My Approach ➔

• Initial Solution: Brute-force approach using extra space--reverse the string and compare with the original.

• Optimization: Explained time and space complexity of the initial approach, then provided an optimized two-pointer solution.

• Execution: Wrote the optimized code, explained it, and performed a dry run with a test case.

V. SQL Query

• Problem: Two tables of sales data were provided.

• Approach: Asked clarifying questions, explained the thought process, and decided to use Joins and GROUP BY to handle multiple entries per customer.

• Solution: Wrote a correct SQL query incorporating both Joins and aggregation functions.

VI. Closing

• The interview concluded with questions about my extracurricular activities.

• I also asked 1-2 questions regarding the company's work culture and upcoming projects.

The interview began with my introduction, during which I introduced myself and briefly summarized my background. They then asked me about my projects, and I provided a concise overview of each. Following this, they inquired about my achievements and participation in hackathons.

They also asked which interview I was currently giving and why I was not selected in previous attempts. The discussion then shifted to TransUnion, where I was asked why I chose the company, what kind of work TransUnion does, and why I wanted to join. They also asked about my position and responsibilities in various committees, including how I mentored juniors and managed my tasks.

Next, the conversation moved to my certifications, including where I completed them and my basic technical knowledge. They also asked why I am switching from Electronics to Tech, my weaknesses, my residence, family, and how I managed extracurricular activities alongside traveling. I was also asked about my career aspirations and where I see myself in the next five years. OA round : 26th July 2025 PPT + Interviews - 29th July 2025 Resume: Deep_Mahesh_Patel.pdf Contact: 9152743762

Placement Process:

1 .OA Round [135 candidates appeared, 37 shortlisted]

The OA consisted of 3 sections, as detailed below:
journey.prep:
● MCQs turned out to be the deciding factor, as most students were able to fully solve the DSA and SQL questions.Focus on practicing MCQs extensively, especially during the final phase of your placement preparation. I personally used GeeksforGeeks and Sanfoundry for preparing Java/C++ MCQs.

● Always make sure to go through the types of questions a company has asked in previous years. This proved to be very helpful for students who had done so for this OA :)

● If you're unable to think of an optimized solution right away, start with a brute-force approach or use the hit-and-trial method. The goal is to pass as many test cases as possible within the limited time, even if the logic isn't the most efficient initially.

● Make sure you have ample sleep before the day of the interview as it is going to be a very long day ahead.

2. Tech Round 1 [37 candidates appeared, 19 Shortlisted] (Lasted around 45 Minutes)

The round began with the typical "Introduce Yourself" question. It is important to plan this thoroughly, as it often sets the tone for the rest of the interview. A well-structured introduction can guide the flow of the conversation toward your strengths and areas you are most comfortable discussing. While introducing yourself, try to subtly highlight any project/internship/competition that might catch the interviewer's interest.

In my case it was a website which I had made for my father's company which automated a lot of repetitive tasks. The interviewer was curious about the same and we went on to discuss it for a couple of minutes.

Next, I was asked to code the classic string permutations problem. Always make sure to explain your thought process and dry run for the same first then start coding. Even while coding, explain each line as you are typing.

Then we had a discussion about some of my other projects in my resume and the interviewer questioned me for my choice of the tech stack for each of them.

The interview concluded with me asking two non-technical company related questions.

Tips:

● In case you are asked a question which you have seen/solved previously, do not make the mistake of directly jumping onto the optimized solution. Start off with the brute force, then go on to explain how you would improve your code to get the most optimal

solution possible. You do not want the interviewer to know that you are already aware about the problem.

● If you are stuck on a question, first explain your approach to the interviewer and ask for hints afterwards. Most of the time, they are interested in your thought process and how well you are able to communicate and understand the problem.

● Have 2-3 unique projects which you can talk hours about. Have the what, why and how prepared for each project ready. It is always a plus if you've worked on a project with real world impact.

● Try to use SQL databases as many times, you might be asked to discuss the schema designs.

3.Techno-HR round [19 candidates appeared] (lasted around 45 minutes)

It was a technical + HR for most of the candidates, but in my case it was completely HR based. The round started again with the introduce yourself question. This time, I made sure to give more emphasis towards my position of responsibilities and the competitions I had taken part in. Following are the questions asked:

● How did I deal with team conflicts that might have occurred during the span of my tenure

● Another question focused on whether I had ever faced a situation where I had to make an unethical decision, and how I dealt with it

● My strengths and weaknesses. (Ensure that you mention the steps you are taking to overcome your weaknesses)

● Where do I see myself in 5 years

● How would I go on to work on a piece of tech that I have little to no idea about

Tips:

● Research about the company values beforehand and try to answer the questions organically in a way which aligns with them, for Barclays, these included RISES principles

● Thoroughly explain your thought process for decision-making questions, including how you weighed the pros and cons in each scenario.

● Try to ask good questions at the end of the interview.This is to ensure that the interviewer remembers you throughout the process

After a long wait, 16 candidates were offered the job.
